source: ESPN injury reports, recorded by RIVL every few hours

3146557:hip.name: Jock Landale
3146557:hip.note: Landale (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
3146557:hip.long: Landale is in danger of missing a fifth consecutive contest due to a left hip strain. If the big man is unable to return Monday, Zuby Ejiofor figures to continue seeing increased burn.

4701230:ankle.name: Jalen Johnson
4701230:ankle.note: Johnson (ankle) is probable for Saturday's game against Brooklyn.
4701230:ankle.long: Johnson has missed each of Atlanta's last three games due to a sprained left ankle, though it seems likely that his string of absences will end Saturday. The 24-year-old has gotten off to another strong start this season, averaging 18.3 points, 9.0 rebounds and 7.9 assists in 32.6 minutes per game.

4712863:foot.name: Mouhamed Gueye
4712863:foot.note: Gueye (foot) is ready to begin on-court activities and will be re-evaluated in four weeks, Brad Rowland of the Locked On Podcast Network reports.
4712863:foot.long: The team stated in July that the big man would remain sidelined for the next 3-to-4 months after undergoing surgery to repair a fractured left foot, and he's continuing to make progress in his rehab. A timetable for Gueye's 2026-27 debut has yet to be established, thought a date could come into focus following his next evaluation in mid-December.

5105571:knee.name: Henri Veesaar
5105571:knee.note: Veesaar was diagnosed with a torn right ACL and is expected to miss the 2026-27 season, the Hawks announced Monday.
5105571:knee.long: Veesaar suffered the injury during a workout on Sept. 15, and an MRI confirmed the diagnosis. The No. 52 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Veesaar was expected to spend a lot of time with Atlanta's G League affiliate this season.

4351852:rest.name: Mitchell Robinson
4351852:rest.note: Robinson (rest) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Magic.
4351852:rest.long: Robinson has been downgraded from questionable to out and will miss the first half of Boston's upcoming back-to-back set. He'll likely be able to suit up Monday in Houston.

4433188:illness.name: Devin Carter
4433188:illness.note: Carter (illness) practiced with the G League's Maine Celtics on Wednesday.
4433188:illness.long: Carter is working back from mononucleosis, which has prevented him from making his season debut. A two-way player, Carter figures to begin his season in Maine as opposed to Boston once healthy.

5101761:rest.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
5101761:rest.note: Brown, who finished with 18 points (5-13 FG, 3-8 3Pt, 5-7 FT), one rebound, three assists and one steal over 25 minutes in Saturday's 124-121 loss to Atlanta, won't play in Sunday's game against Dallas, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5101761:rest.long: Brown logged his fifth consecutive double-digit scoring performance Saturday. However, his efforts weren't enough to help the Nets hold off a late Hawks comeback and earn their third win of the 2026-27 campaign. Head coach Jordi Fernandez mentioned after the game that the rookie won't suit up Sunday versus the Mavericks, the second game of a back-to-back. Without Brown in the lineup, Terance Mann should see more minutes off the bench. Keon Ellis, who didn't get on the floor versus Atlanta, might also get involved.

5175643:leg.name: Egor Demin
5175643:leg.note: Demin (leg) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Pelicans, Erik Slater of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5175643:leg.long: Brian Lewis of the New York Post reported earlier Tuesday that Demin practiced as well. With Demin previously sidelined by a right leg bone bruise, this designation suggests he is trending toward returning to Brooklyn's backcourt Wednesday. If he is cleared to play, the guard would be in position to reclaim the top spot at point guard.

5105626:shoulder.name: Tyler Bilodeau
5105626:shoulder.note: Bilodeau (shoulder) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against Indiana.
5105626:shoulder.long: Bilodeau will miss a third straight game to begin the regular season due to a right shoulder sprain. The two-way player's absence shouldn't affect the rotation.

5061575:hamstring.name: Kon Knueppel
5061575:hamstring.note: Knueppel (hamstring) was diagnosed with a left hamstring strain Sunday and will be re-evaluated in four weeks.
5061575:hamstring.long: Knueppel missed the first eight games of the 2026-27 campaign. He returned for the 114-104 loss to Brooklyn on Wednesday, though he exited the contest after just six minutes of work and didn't return. With Knueppel out of commission for at least a month, Grayson Allen and Sion James are candidates to replace him in the starting lineup, especially with Dennis Schroder (hamstring) sidelined for a minimum of two weeks.

4395651:calf.name: Coby White
4395651:calf.note: White (calf) is probable for Wednesday's game in Brooklyn.
4395651:calf.long: White came out of his regular-season debut unscathed and should be available for Wednesday's game. White saw 16 minutes of action in Monday's 124-91 loss to the Pistons, but he should be cleared for more playing time in his second game of the season.

4066218:hamstring.name: Grant Williams
4066218:hamstring.note: Williams (hamstring) is listed as probable for Thursday's game against the Suns.
4066218:hamstring.long: Williams is trending toward making his season debut Thursday after battling a right hamstring strain. However, the veteran forward isn't guaranteed to see meaningful playing time once he returns.

4684269:knee.name: Kylan Boswell
4684269:knee.note: Boswell (knee) is out for Wednesday's season opener against the Nets.
4684269:knee.long: Boswell continues to rehab after right knee surgery. The hope in early October was that he would be cleared for basketball activities prior to the start of the G League season, which begins in early November.

4848625:back.name: Dailyn Swain
4848625:back.note: Swain (back) is out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
4848625:back.long: Swain will miss his second game in a row, with this one being the front end of a back-to-back set. He can be considered questionable for Saturday against the Timberwolves.

4278067:hamstring.name: Nic Claxton
4278067:hamstring.note: Claxton (hamstring) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against the 76ers.
4278067:hamstring.long: Collins was originally marked as probable for Sunday's contest, but he appears to be trending in the wrong direction as game day approaches. If Claxton needs to sit out another game, Jalen Smith (hand) would presumably continue to operate as the Bulls' starting center.

4683747:ankle.name: Jaylon Tyson
4683747:ankle.note: Tyson (ankle) is questionable to face the Knicks on Wednesday.
4683747:ankle.long: Tyson has been out since spraining his right ankle on Oct. 30, but it looks like there's a chance he could return Wednesday. If he can get back out there, Meleek Thomas' minutes would likely dip.

5279129:knee.name: Sergio de Larrea
5279129:knee.note: De Larrea (knee) has been ruled out for Thursday's game at Minnesota.
5279129:knee.long: De Larrea hasn't played since Oct. 26 due to a right knee sprain, but he's expected to be re-evaluated soon. Still, he can be considered week-to-week until Dallas provides an update on his progress.

4593125:knee.name: Santi Aldama
4593125:knee.note: Aldama (knee) is probable to suit up for Friday's game against the Jazz.
4593125:knee.long: Aldama has missed the first eight games of the season while recovering from right knee surgery in March. Getting upgraded to probable is a good sign the former Grizzlies forward will be ready to make his Mavericks debut at home against Utah. Aldama will likely begin the campaign on a minutes restriction, but his return probably means less minutes for Zaccharie Risacher and Morez Johnson Jr.

5148538:heel.name: Tarik Biberovic
5148538:heel.note: Biberovic (heel) is out for Thursday's game against Minnesota.
5148538:heel.long: Biberovic remains plagued by right heel bursitis. The rookie forward carries no timetable for his season debut.

4683688:foot.name: Dereck Lively II
4683688:foot.note: Lively (foot) is listed as out for Thursday's game in Minnesota.
4683688:foot.long: Lively is still working his way back from foot surgery. He's reportedly trending favorably, though he should continue to be classified as week-to-week, at least until the team provides an update. While Lively remains on the shelf, Daniel Gafford is expected to stay in the starting lineup, with Morez Johnson (shin), Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse all in line to spend time at the five when needed.

4065813:personal.name: Alpha Diallo
4065813:personal.note: Diallo (personal/wrist) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Phoenix, Vic Lombardi of Altitude Sports reports.
4065813:personal.long: Diallo will miss a fourth consecutive contest while attending to a personal matter. He's also dealing with a right wrist sprain. The 29-year-old's next opportunity to return to action will come Monday against the Trail Blazers.

4592427:hamstring.name: Spencer Jones
4592427:hamstring.note: Jones (hamstring) is out for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
4592427:hamstring.long: Jones is still battling bilateral hamstring problems. He can be considered out indefinitely until the Nuggets offer another update on his recovery.

4432181:knee.name: Julian Strawther
4432181:knee.note: Strawther (knee) was diagnosed with a left knee sprain Friday and will be re-evaluated in six weeks, Vinny Benedetto of The Denver Gazette reports.
4432181:knee.long: Strawther suffered the injury in Wednesday's preseason game against the Clippers. The 24-year-old has appeared in 172 regular-season games for the Nuggets since entering the league in 2023, averaging 7.1 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 16.2 minutes per contest. He was in line to compete for an expanded role during the 2026-27 campaign. While that may be the case once Strawther is cleared to suit up, Tyus Jones and potentially Ryan Nembhard are candidates to receive more minutes in the interim.

4395702:hip.name: Isaiah Joe
4395702:hip.note: Joe (hip) is out for Monday against the Wizards.
4395702:hip.long: Joe is missing a seventh consecutive contest with a bruised hip. His next chance to play comes Thursday in a road rematch with Washington.

4433621:hamstring.name: Jalen Duren
4433621:hamstring.note: Duren (hamstring) has begun on-court activity and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Hunter Patterson of The Athletic reports.
4433621:hamstring.long: Duren is progressing in his rehab after suffering a right hamstring strain Oct. 23, though he'll remain on the inactive list for at least the next two weeks while ramping up toward a return to game action. Paul Reed should continue to play a sizable role in Duren's stead.

4997536:knee.name: Gui Santos
4997536:knee.note: Santos (knee) is listed as probable for Monday's game against New Orleans.
4997536:knee.long: Santos' knee issue isn't anything new, so he'll be on the floor Monday, barring a setback. The 24-year-old has appeared in seven regular-season games in 2026-27, averaging 6.6 points, 3.6 rebounds and 1.1 assists over 18.9 minutes per contest.

6589:rest.name: Draymond Green
6589:rest.note: Green (back) is out for Sunday's game against the Clippers.
6589:rest.long: Green will sit out the first leg of this back-to-back set, but he should return for Monday's game against the Suns. Graham Ike, Al Horford and Charles Bassey will help pick up the slack with Green inactive Sunday.

3975:rest.name: Stephen Curry
3975:rest.note: Curry (rest) won't play Sunday against the Clippers, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
3975:rest.long: Sunday's game will be the first of a back-to-back set, so Curry will receive a maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Suns. De'Anthony Melton could draw the start sans Curry, and Brandin Podziemski will be more involved in the offense.

3102531:illness.name: Kristaps Porzingis
3102531:illness.note: Porzingis announced on his social media that he's stepping away from basketball.
3102531:illness.long: Porzingis said he was looking forward to joining the Warriors, but his body didn't respond the way he wanted it too during his ramp-up process before the season. Additionally, he said he will work with the Warriors on a solution that "makes sense." Porzingis is making this decision to prioritize his health and will hopefully turn a corner soon on that front.

4432171:knee.name: Moses Moody
4432171:knee.note: Moody (knee) is progressing toward a potential return between December and January after rupturing his left patellar tendon in March, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
4432171:knee.long: Moody has been limited to individual court work, but team sources indicate he's ahead of Jimmy Butler (knee) in the rehabilitation process and is expected to return before the veteran forward. The 24-year-old still has several recovery checkpoints to complete, and Golden State has not established an official timetable. His eventual return would help replenish a Warriors wing rotation that will open the season without both Moody and Butler.

6430:knee.name: Jimmy Butler III
6430:knee.note: Butler (knee) could return sometime between January and February as he continues recovering from a torn right ACL, Anthony Slater of ESPN reports.
6430:knee.long: Butler, who underwent surgery after suffering the injury Jan. 19, has progressed to individual court work but still has several rehabilitation milestones to clear. His next step involves landing comfortably after a game-speed jump. Coach Steve Kerr is hopeful Butler can rejoin Golden State for the latter portion of the season, though no official return date has been announced. The 37-year-old forward remains a significant part of the Warriors' plans and could provide a substantial boost during the second half of the campaign.

2991230:knee.name: Fred VanVleet
2991230:knee.note: VanVleet (knee) won't play Saturday against the Thunder.
2991230:knee.long: It's the second night of a back-to-back set, so VanVleet will receive his standard maintenance day, but he should return for Monday's meeting with the Celtics. Reed Sheppard (back) is also out for Saturday's game, so Marcus Smart could draw the start at point guard, and Amen Thompson should see some increased playmaking responsibilities.

4711272:back.name: Reed Sheppard
4711272:back.note: Sheppard (back) is questionable for Monday's game against the Celtics.
4711272:back.long: Sheppard is in danger of missing his fourth game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Fred VanVleet (knee) not listed on the injury report, Marcus Smart could continue to be more involved than usual if Sheppard can't suit up Monday.

2991235:calf.name: Steven Adams
2991235:calf.note: Head coach Ime Udoka said Monday that Adams could return as soon as Sunday's game at Washington, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
2991235:calf.long: The veteran center is still recovering from a right soleus strain and hasn't played since Oct. 23. With Adams and Clint Capela (ankle) both sidelined, Tari Eason and Jabari Smith figure to see increased burn at center.

4017837:ankle.name: Ivica Zubac
4017837:ankle.note: Zubac (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
4017837:ankle.long: Zubac has missed the last five regular-season games due to an ankle injury. While it's not clear how healthy he is, the questionable designation at least suggests he's moving in the right direction. If Zubac is sidelined again Wednesday versus Memphis, Jay Huff is expected to remain in the starting lineup at the five.

4396909:hamstring.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:hamstring.note: Nesmith (hamstring) is listed as probable for Sunday's game against Brooklyn.
4396909:hamstring.long: Nesmith didn't play in the 123-120 loss to New Orleans on Opening Night but has played in each of the Pacers' last five contests. Although he could see limited action while he continues to work his way back from the left hamstring strain, he will likely be out there Sunday, barring a setback.

4278355:back.name: Obi Toppin
4278355:back.note: Toppin (back) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
4278355:back.long: Toppin was available for emergency purposes Monday against the Hawks, so he figures to have a good chance of playing Wednesday. The Pacers should update his status closer to tipoff.

2530530:hamstring.name: T.J. McConnell
2530530:hamstring.note: McConnell is probable for Friday's game against the Knicks due to a right hamstring strain.
2530530:hamstring.long: McConnell continues to land on the injury report with a hamstring issue, but it's a positive sign that he's been listed as probable after being handed a questionable tag ahead of Indiana's previous three games. He's in line to play in a fourth consecutive game after logging a season high in minutes (14) Wednesday night against Washington.

5157066:knee.name: Johnny Furphy
5157066:knee.note: Furphy (knee) is practicing with the G League's Noblesville Boom, per Alex Golden of SI.com.
5157066:knee.long: The Pacers have been pretty quiet regarding Furphy's ACL recovery since the offseason, but it's encouraging to hear some form of progress as the forward begins to ramp up his activity. Although Furphy still lacks a firm timetable for a return and is likely to be brought back slowly, it appears a season debut before the start of the new calendar year is in the cards.

4433076:knee.name: Ben Sheppard
4433076:knee.note: Head coach Rick Carlise confirmed Sheppard will miss "months" after undergoing surgery to repair a torn meniscus in his left knee, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
4433076:knee.long: Sheppard required a full repair and is without a definitive timetable for a return to action. With Tyrese Haliburton (hamstring) expected to miss at least two weeks, Quenton Jackson figures to see a significant uptick in playing time. Two-way player Braden Smith could also see increased action with the parent club.

4396993:hamstring.name: Tyrese Haliburton
4396993:hamstring.note: Head coach Rick Carlisle said Wednesday that Haliburton (hamstring) will miss at least 10 more days, Alex Golden of SI.com reports.
4396993:hamstring.long: Haliburton is still recovering from a left hamstring strain and will need more time to ramp up. Andrew Nembhard should continue seeing increased on-ball duties in Haliburton's stead, while Quenton Jackson and Braden Smith are also candidates for increased burn.

5108024:foot.name: Yanic Konan Niederhauser
5108024:foot.note: Niederhauser (foot) is out for Tuesday's game against Phoenix, Ohm Youngmisuk of ESPN.com reports.
5108024:foot.long: Niederhauser has yet to make an appearance this season for the Clippers while rehabbing from foot surgery. It's unclear at this time when he'll be available to take the court, and he can be considered week-to-week until further notice.

4065778:foot.name: Max Strus
4065778:foot.note: Strus (foot) practiced and participated in 5-on-5 with the San Diego Clippers on Saturday, Los Angeles Clippers sideline reporter/host Ohm Youngmisuk reports.
4065778:foot.long: Strus continues to progress in his recovery from a partially torn plantar fascia in his right foot suffered in the Clippers' preseason opener. He'll keep working with the G League affiliate and will likely play his first minutes of the season there before he's cleared to return to the NBA level.

3913176:achilles.name: Brandon Ingram
3913176:achilles.note: Ingram (Achilles) won't play in Friday's game against the Thunder, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
3913176:achilles.long: Ingram is ramping up his activity as he nears his season debut for the Clippers, but he's not yet cleared for game action amid his Achilles rehab. Until the star forward is ready to suit up, Kris Dunn, Rui Hachimura and Derrick Jones should all hang onto starting roles.

6580:knee.name: Bradley Beal
6580:knee.note: Beal (knee) will not be ready for the start of the regular season, NBA writer Justin Russo reports.
6580:knee.long: Beal is dealing with knee inflammation that will keep him sidelined for Opening Night. While it's unclear how long the Clippers will be without the veteran guard, Darius Garland, Keaton Wagler and Kris Dunn should dominate the backcourt minutes in his absence. Beal's 2025-26 campaign was cut short by a hip injury after he averaged 8.2 points and 1.7 assists in 20.6 minutes across just six regular-season appearances.

4396818:shoulder.name: Jordan Miller
4396818:shoulder.note: Miller underwent surgery Wednesday to repair a torn left rotator cuff and will be re-evaluated in six months, per Law Murray of The Athletic.
4396818:shoulder.long: It's a tough break for Miller, who had an opportunity to battle for a reserve role during training camp in the fall. The timeline for a return is likely to keep him on the shelf until after the All-Star break. Miller's extended stay on the sidelines gives Kobe Sanders a chance to crack the Clippers' rotation.

4433137:foot.name: Ziaire Williams
4433137:foot.note: Williams (foot) is out for Sunday's game against the Raptors.
4433137:foot.long: Williams will now miss his third consecutive outing as he recovers from a left foot injury. Jake LaRavia is in line for a second straight start, while Quentin Grimes and Sandro Mamukelashvili should continue to see an uptick in minutes off the bench.

5060631:knee.name: Adou Thiero
5060631:knee.note: The Lakers recalled Thiero (knee) from the G League's Coachella Valley Lakers on Thursday, per Ryan Ward of SI.com.
5060631:knee.long: Thiero was practicing with the G League club amid his knee recovery. He looks to be on the verge of being cleared for his season debut with the Lakers.

4593016:ankle.name: Quinten Post
4593016:ankle.note: Post (ankle) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Indiana.
4593016:ankle.long: Post is in danger of missing his third consecutive contest because of a right ankle sprain. If Post remains sidelined Wednesday versus the Pacers, Kris Murray should continue to see more minutes.

4431785:back.name: Scotty Pippen Jr.
4431785:back.note: Pippen (back) remains out for Wednesday's game against Denver, Michael Wallace of the Grizzlies' official site reports.
4431785:back.long: With Pippen set to miss another game, Memphis will continue to operate without one of its backcourt reserves. He has now been sidelined for six straight contests due to the back issue and can be considered week-to-week until Memphis offers an update on his recovery. Cam Spencer remains worth streaming in most fantasy leagues.

4065733:back.name: Ty Jerome
4065733:back.note: Jerome (back) won't play in Saturday's game versus Sacramento, Chris Herrington of The Daily Memphian.
4065733:back.long: Jerome has been battling a nagging back injury, though it will finally force him to miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. With Scotty Pippen (back) also sidelined, Cam Spencer is the favorite to start at the one.

3032976:back.name: Rudy Gobert
3032976:back.note: Gobert (back) is out for Saturday's game against the Spurs, Dane Moore of 'The Dane Moore NBA Podcast' reports.
3032976:back.long: Gobert will miss his first game of the season Saturday, which could result in Joan Beringer getting the start and Trey Lyles could see a bump in minutes. For now, Gobert should be considered questionable for Monday's meeting with Milwaukee.

4594268:knee.name: Anthony Edwards
4594268:knee.note: Edwards underwent a successful arthroscopic procedure on his right knee Thursday, the Timberwolves announced.
4594268:knee.long: Edwards underwent debridement surgery in Minnesota, though the team did not provide a timetable for his return. The star guard is expected to make a full recovery, with additional updates coming as he progresses through rehabilitation. Based on previous reporting from ESPN's Shams Charania, Edwards could miss up to two months. Edwards was off to a scorching start this season, averaging 33.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 2.0 steals across four appearances.

3934673:achilles.name: Donte DiVincenzo
3934673:achilles.note: DiVincenzo (Achilles) remains confident that he'll return during the 2026-27 season, Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reports.
3934673:achilles.long: DiVincenzo is approaching six months since tearing his right Achilles during the first round of the playoffs and has been rehabbing with the expectation that he'll play at some point this season. The veteran guard has sought advice from Jayson Tatum, Tyrese Haliburton and Damian Lillard during his recovery, though Minnesota has yet to establish a timetable for his return.

4277956:ankle.name: Jordan Poole
4277956:ankle.note: Poole (ankle) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Utah.
4277956:ankle.long: Poole is expected to return from a three-game layoff for the meeting with the Jazz on Wednesday. The 27-year-old hasn't had a memorable 2026-27 campaign thus far, averaging 6.0 points, 2.0 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.3 steals across 16.0 minutes per contest. If Poole is cleared for action, it would likely mean fewer minutes for Bryce McGowens and Trendon Watford.

3907497:personal.name: Dejounte Murray
3907497:personal.note: Murray (personal) is out for Monday's game against the Grizzlies.
3907497:personal.long: Murray remains away from the team due to the birth of his son. His next opportunity to return will come Wednesday against the Jazz. Jeremiah Fears should be in line for another start at point guard with Murray and Jordan Poole (ankle) sidelined.

5061589:knee.name: Yves Missi
5061589:knee.note: Missi (knee) is out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
5061589:knee.long: Even though Missi has been trending in the right direction and was recently cleared to resume on-court activities, this game will come too soon for him. This means Missi will miss an 11th consecutive game while dealing with a left knee bone bruise. His next chance to play will come Saturday against the Nuggets, and in the meantime, Karlo Matkovic will remain in the starting lineup.

4277869:ankle.name: Jose Alvarado
4277869:ankle.note: Alvarado (ankle) is questionable for Monday's game against the Nets.
4277869:ankle.long: Alvarado has missed four straight games and was ruled out at least 24 hours in advance of each absence. However, it appears he's nearing a return to action. If available Monday, Alvarado would likely face limitations, while Jordan Clarkson and Tyler Kolek would be candidates for fewer minutes.

4683692:shoulder.name: Cason Wallace
4683692:shoulder.note: Wallace underwent surgery Friday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
4683692:shoulder.long: Wallace is expected to miss most, if not all, of the season. However, there's still a chance he will return late in the campaign after sustaining the shoulder injury in Sunday's win over the Clippers. With Jalen Williams (leg) also set to be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Alex Caruso (ankle) should see significant playing time once cleared to return. In the meantime, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Josh Dix are expected to see increased burn.

4433255:knee.name: Chet Holmgren
4433255:knee.note: Holmgren underwent a biological treatment Friday to address a small patellar tendon tear and will miss at least 8-10 weeks, Nick Crain of Slam reports.
4433255:knee.long: This is another massive blow to an Oklahoma City squad that's already set to be without Jalen Williams (leg) and Cason Wallace (shoulder) for most, if not all, of the season. With Holmgren sidelined, Kenrich Williams, Jaylin Williams and Aday Mara are all candidates to see increased playing time. Two-way player Brooks Barnhizer could also see more minutes.

4593803:leg.name: Jalen Williams
4593803:leg.note: Williams (leg) underwent successful surgery Wednesday to "address a fractured left fibula and reconstruction of ankle ligaments following a fracture and dislocation." He will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, Tim MacMahon of ESPN.com reports.
4593803:leg.long: Williams suffered the injury during Sunday's meeting with the Clippers and was taken off the court on a stretcher. It's unknown when the 25-year-old will be cleared to return, though the Thunder will presumably be overly cautious moving forward. Williams, who signed a five-year extension in July of 2025, has had a productive career, averaging 17.9 points, 4.6 rebounds, 4.4 assists and 1.3 steals over 30.9 minutes per contest. However, after playing at least 69 regular-season games in his first three years in the league, he has appeared in just 36 in the last two seasons combined. With the Thunder having one of the deepest rosters in the NBA, the team may look for more minutes from Jared McCain, Jaylin Williams, and Kenrich Williams for the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign.

2991350:ankle.name: Alex Caruso
2991350:ankle.note: Caruso (ankle) is expected to miss time due to an ankle sprain, Clemente Almanza of USA Today reports.
2991350:ankle.long: With Caruso already ruled out for Wednesday's game in Dallas due to an ankle sprain, it sounds like the veteran forward could remain sidelined beyond a one-game absence. That would leave Oklahoma City without one of its key rotation wings for at least the near term, which could force Jared McCain into a big role for the banged-up Thunder.

5061603:knee.name: Thomas Sorber
5061603:knee.note: Sorber (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
5061603:knee.long: Sorber is still recovering from knee surgery and remains without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Thunder offer an update on his status.

5159925:back.name: Nikola Topic
5159925:back.note: Topic (back) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
5159925:back.long: Topic has yet to play during the 2026-27 campaign, and at this rate, it doesn't look like he will be on the floor anytime soon. For now, he should be considered week-to-week. The 2024 No. 12 overall pick has appeared in only 10 regular-season games throughout his career, averaging 5.2 points, 1.9 rebounds and 4.4 assists while shooting 40.0 percent from deep over 16.0 minutes per contest.

4065654:knee.name: Jonathan Isaac
4065654:knee.note: Isaac (knee) is out for Tuesday's game against Sacramento.
4065654:knee.long: Isaac has yet to make his 2026-27 debut while continuing his rehab from a left knee injury. His next opportunity to take the court will arrive Wednesday in Utah.

4432165:knee.name: Jalen Suggs
4432165:knee.note: Suggs (knee) participated in Friday's morning shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
4432165:knee.long: With Suggs having already been listed as questionable entering the day, his participation in shootaround is another positive sign in his recovery from the right knee bone bruise. He's trending in the right direction, but a final call on his availability will be made closer to the 7 p.m.ET tipoff.

4432573:ankle.name: Paolo Banchero
4432573:ankle.note: Banchero is expected to be sidelined for the next four-to-six weeks due to a right high-ankle sprain, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4432573:ankle.long: Banchero left during Friday's loss against the Timberwolves due to an ankle injury, and follow-up tests have confirmed a high-ankle sprain for the fifth-year forward. With an extended absence expected, the Magic will have to rely more heavily on Franz Wagner and Desmond Bane offensively, and Tristan da Silva figures to be the top candidate to enter the Magic's starting lineup for as long as Banchero is sidelined.

5214637:hamstring.name: Noah Penda
5214637:hamstring.note: Penda was diagnosed with a partially torn right hamstring Saturday, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
5214637:hamstring.long: Penda suffered the hamstring tear in Friday's 136-115 preseason win over the Heat. It's unknown how long the injury will keep the 21-year-old off the floor. However, since it's a different injury than the one he suffered in the same hamstring during training camp, the team may take a cautious approach regarding his return. Penda, the No. 32 overall pick in the 2025 NBA Draft, averaged 3.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 assists over 12.8 minutes per outing in 59 regular-season games in 2025-26. While he's not expected to be a mainstay in the rotation throughout the 2026-27 campaign, his absence could open up a few minutes for Tristan Da Silva.

5107251:ankle.name: Izaiyah Nelson
5107251:ankle.note: Team president Jeff Weltman said Monday that Nelson (ankle) remains about a month away from returning to the court after offseason surgery, per Philip Rossman-Reich of OrlandoMagicDaily.com.
5107251:ankle.long: With Nelson still in recovery mode from the left ankle surgery he underwent this summer, his path back to game action remains delayed for the early part of the season. The rookie big man is on a two-way contract with the Magic, so his short-term absence mainly affects his developmental timeline rather than Orlando's regular rotation.

3059318:foot.name: Joel Embiid
3059318:foot.note: Embiid (foot) remains questionable for Thursday's game against the Raptors, but he participated in the team's morning shootaround, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
3059318:foot.long: Embiid and LeBron James (back) are trending in the right direction after drawing questionable tags, but their availability has yet to be determined, with the superstar big man saying he has "no idea" if he's going to be playing Thursday. Even if Embiid is cleared to play against the Raptors, it's likely that he'll miss at least one game during the 76ers' upcoming Sunday-Monday back-to-back set.

1966:back.name: LeBron James
1966:back.note: James (back) is out for Thursday's game against Toronto.
1966:back.long: The future Hall of Famer is getting Thursday night off for maintenace purposes. Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown should do the heavy lifting offensively, while Dean Wade and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope should soak up extra minutes for the 76ers.

4870562:back.name: Dominick Barlow
4870562:back.note: Barlow (back) participated in Thursday's shootaround but doesn't have a timeline to return to game action, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
4870562:back.long: Barlow has been dealing with back soreness dating back to the preseason, so his participation in shootaround is an encouraging step. However, the 76ers have yet to provide a firm return date, and he'll likely need to ramp up further before he's cleared to play. Barlow should be monitored in deeper formats, but he isn't someone who needs to be rostered while he remains sidelined.

4871141:achilles.name: Ariel Hukporti
4871141:achilles.note: Hukporti has sustained a season-ending ruptured right Achilles tendon, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4871141:achilles.long: Hukporti went down with an Achilles injury in Monday's preseason opener against the Knicks, and an MRI has since revealed a rupture. He signed a one-year deal with the 76ers over the summer, so Hukporti will be an unrestricted free agent come season's end. With Hukporti's year already finished, Adem Bona (foot) should assume the backup center role behind Joel Embiid once healthy.

4701232:shoulder.name: Mark Williams
4701232:shoulder.note: Williams underwent surgery Thursday to repair a torn labrum in his left shoulder and will miss an extended period of time, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4701232:shoulder.long: This is a tough blow for the center with training camp right around the corner. With his status for Opening Night in jeopardy, this will put a lot of eyes on Oso Ighodaro and Khaman Maluach, with the latter already drawing buzz during the Summer League. More clarity on Williams' timeline should be known in the coming weeks.

4279888:hamstring.name: Ja Morant
4279888:hamstring.note: Head coach Micah Nori said Morant met with a doctor in Los Angeles, who gave him a positive outlook on his recovery from the hamstring injury. While Nori declined to update Morant's timetable, he added Morant "may not be out for as long as we thought," Trail Blazers Insider Sean Highkin reports.
4279888:hamstring.long: Morant was initially given a four-week timetable after he suffered a Grade 2 left hamstring strain on Oct. 30. It sounds like he's making solid progress, though it would be surprising to see him beat that timetable given the tricky nature of hamstring injuries. Scoot Henderson will continue to start in his absence and there will be more minutes available for Jrue Holiday.

4914336:knee.name: Shaedon Sharpe
4914336:knee.note: Sharpe suffered a torn meniscus in his knee and is expected to miss six months, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4914336:knee.long: It's a tough blow to the Trail Blazers' depth on the wing ahead of training camp. Sharpe, who is now likely to be sidelined until after the All-Star break, had been ticketed for a reserve role behind Toumani Camara following an injury-plagued 2025-26 campaign, which saw average a career-high 20.8 points, 1.4 steals and 2.1 three-pointers per game over 50 regular-season appearances. The door is now open for Vit Krejci and Jeremy Sochan to compete for bench minutes during camp.

4433174:calf.name: Dylan Cardwell
4433174:calf.note: Cardwell (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Mavericks.
4433174:calf.long: Cardwell was temporarily upgraded to probable ahead of Monday's clash, though he was downgraded twice before ultimately being ruled out with a left calf strain. His next chance to make his season debut will arrive Wednesday against the Lakers.

4898371:knee.name: Maxime Raynaud
4898371:knee.note: Raynaud (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Orlando.
4898371:knee.long: Raynaud is expected to be re-evaluated soon, though he can be considered week-to-week until the Kings offer an update on his status. Dylan Cardwell and Precious Achiuwa will likely continue seeing increased burn in Raynaud's absence.

4594327:ankle.name: Keegan Murray
4594327:ankle.note: Murray (ankle) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Heat.
4594327:ankle.long: Murray hasn't played since going down with an ankle injury on Oct. 25, so if he is cleared for Sunday's game, his minutes will likely be monitored. His return would likely push Precious Achiuwa back to the second unit.

3907387:achilles.name: Ben Simmons
3907387:achilles.note: Simmons underwent successful surgery Tuesday to repair a torn right Achilles tendon, James Ham of ESPN 1320 Sacramento reports.
3907387:achilles.long: Simmons had a quality preseason, averaging 10.5 points, 4.0 rebounds and 4.0 assists over 17.4 minutes per contest (two games). The 30-year-old was on track to suit up for the Kings on opening night, though those plans were halted after he suffered a torn Achilles tendon during practice. Now, Simmons will focus on rehab. However, it's unknown what the future holds regarding his career in the NBA.

6440:calf.name: Tobias Harris
6440:calf.note: Harris (calf) is out for Wednesday's game against Chicago, Jared Weiss of The Athletic reports.
6440:calf.long: With Harris still sidelined, San Antonio will rely more on Julian Champagnie. Harris has yet to make his Spurs debut this season, so his absence continues to leave minutes available on the wing until he is cleared to return.

5101845:knee.name: Jayden Quaintance
5101845:knee.note: Quaintance has been around the team but has not yet been cleared for basketball activities, Matt Guzman of SI.com reports.
5101845:knee.long: The Spurs are expected to exercise extreme caution with the big man, as Quaintance suffered a torn ACL and meniscus with Arizona State in February 2025 before appearing in only four games with Kentucky last season due to severe complications and persistent swelling. The 19-year-old underwent a cleanup procedure on his meniscus in mid-July, and the Spurs will likely want him at 100 percent before ramping him up to basketball activities.

6450:knee.name: Kawhi Leonard
6450:knee.note: Head coach Darko Rajakovic said Wednesday that Leonard (knee) is doing individual on-court work and is progressing well, Michael Grange of Sportsnet.ca reports.
6450:knee.long: The Raptors are expected to provide another update on Leonard's status in about one week, though it's encouraging to see how he's progressed thus far. Collin Murray-Boyles and Ja'Kobe Walter are candidates for increased playing time for as long as Leonard is sidelined.

4432586:foot.name: Nate Bittle
4432586:foot.note: Bittle (foot) is listed as out for Monday's game against Memphis.
4432586:foot.long: Bittle has been battling a foot injury for a couple of months. It's unknown when the rookie will be cleared to suit up for the Raptors, so he should be considered week-to-week for now.

4277961:knee.name: Jaren Jackson Jr.
4277961:knee.note: Jackson has been diagnosed with a torn MCL in his right knee and will be sidelined for 6-to-8 weeks, per Shams Charania of ESPN.
4277961:knee.long: Jackson sustained the injury early in Monday's loss to Memphis, and he's now expected to miss at least a month and a half of action. The star big man's absence creates a major void in the Utah lineup, one that is likely to be filled by a timeshare of Jaxson Hayes (shoulder), Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba. The Jazz could also shift Lauri Markkanen (wrist), when healthy, to the center spot at times, perhaps allowing Ace Bailey to spend more time at power forward.

4433268:knee.name: Trey Alexander
4433268:knee.note: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
4433268:knee.long: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

3102530:foot.name: Jusuf Nurkic
3102530:foot.note: Nurkic (toe) has begun participating in on-court activities as he continues recovering from a right foot injury sustained during an Oct. 4 preseason game against Denver. He will be re-evaluated in two weeks, the Jazz announced Friday.
3102530:foot.long: Nurkic is progressing in his recovery, but the two-week re-evaluation timeline indicates he remains some distance from returning to game action. His absence should continue to create opportunities in Utah's frontcourt, with Jaxson Hayes and Mo Bamba among the players positioned to benefit from additional playing time. Nurkic's next evaluation will provide a clearer picture of his potential return date.

4432907:foot.name: Justin Champagnie
4432907:foot.note: Champagnie (foot) is expected to miss several months, per Josh Robbins of The Athletic.
4432907:foot.long: The forward underwent surgery Wednesday to address a fractured foot, and the Wizards hope Champagnie will be ready to return at some time around the All-Star break in February. The likes of Bilal Coulibaly, Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington will all be asked to help pick up the slack for the foreseeable future.

4997537:hip.name: Tristan Vukcevic
4997537:hip.note: Vukcevic (hip) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Detroit.
4997537:hip.long: Vukcevic has yet to make his season debut due to a left hip impingement. The big man can be viewed as week-to-week until the Wizards provide an update on his progress.

4606840:knee.name: Jamir Watkins
4606840:knee.note: The Wizards announced Thursday that Watkins has undergone surgery for a torn ACL.
4606840:knee.long: Watkins, a two-way player for the Wizards, suffered the injury during the Summer League. Although Washington has yet to offer a timetable for a return, a typical recovery time for the procedure is approximately 9-to-12 months. That leaves Watkins in serious jeopardy of missing most, if not all, of the 2026-27 season, and it remains to be seen if the team will continue keeping him around on a two-way roster spot while he's injured.

4397189:finger.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:finger.note: Smith (finger) is probable for Sunday's game against Philadelphia.
4397189:finger.long: Smith left Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks after just seven minutes of play due to a left finger sprain and was initially deemed questionable for Sunday. His upgraded status is a good sign for Smith, who's been the starting center with Nic Claxton (hamstring) yet to play this season.

5105555:ankle.name: Tobe Awaka
5105555:ankle.note: Awaka (ankle) is probable for Monday's game against Philadelphia.
5105555:ankle.long: Awaka played 12 minutes during Friday's 125-111 loss to the Celtics after missing one game with the ankle issue. The rookie big man will continue to provide depth off the bench for the Bulls behind Jalen Smith.

4576087:hamstring.name: Peyton Watson
4576087:hamstring.note: Watson (hamstring) is questionable for Friday's game against the 76ers.
4576087:hamstring.long: Watson has missed his team's last two matchups due to a hamstring issue, and he's in danger of missing a third Friday. More information on his availability should come to light as tipoff nears.

6442:knee.name: Kyrie Irving
6442:knee.note: Irving (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Kings.
6442:knee.long: Irving was initially listed as questionable before being downgraded to doubtful Monday afternoon, and he's since been ruled out. With the star floor general sidelined, Marcus Sasser and Walter Clayton are candidates for increased burn, while Cooper Flagg will likely see increased playmaking duties.

4065813:wrist.name: Alpha Diallo
4065813:wrist.note: Diallo (wrist) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Raptors.
4065813:wrist.long: Diallo played through the wrist issue Monday and logged six minutes off the bench in a 118-110 loss to Portland. He should see a similar workload Wednesday.

3102529:ankle.name: Clint Capela
3102529:ankle.note: Head coach Ime Udoka stated Monday that Capela (ankle) could be cleared to return either Nov. 15 in Washington or Nov. 16 in Miami, Lachard Binkley of SI.com reports.
3102529:ankle.long: Capela is missing a fourth straight game Monday against Denver due to a right ankle sprain, but he appears to be trending in the right direction. He'll presumably need to log 5-on-5 work before gaining clearance to play, though the Rockets haven't disclosed how far along the big man is in his rehab.

2528210:personal.name: Tim Hardaway Jr.
2528210:personal.note: Hardaway (personal) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Lakers.
2528210:personal.long: Hardaway is dealing with a personal issue and is in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 campaign. If he can't suit up Monday in Los Angeles, Dru Smith and Nikola Jovic should see more minutes.

4397688:knee.name: Trey Murphy III
4397688:knee.note: Murphy (knee) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
4397688:knee.long: Murphy will miss a third consecutive game while nursing bilateral patellar tendinopathy. He'll aim to return in the second leg of this back-to-back set against the Nuggets on Saturday. Saddiq Bey should continue to see an expanded role with Murphy on the sidelines.

3064440:elbow.name: Zach LaVine
3064440:elbow.note: LaVine (elbow) is questionable to play in Monday's game against Dallas.
3064440:elbow.long: LaVine played a season-low 21 minutes during Saturday's 136-105 loss to Memphis, but it's unclear if that was due to the elbow soreness or the game being out of reach for the Kings. Either way, his status will bear monitoring ahead of Monday's clash with the Mavericks. If he's unable to play, Darius Acuff Jr.'s usage would skyrocket, while Malik Monk, Emanuel Sharp and Nique Clifford could all see increased opportunities in the backcourt.

5160992:knee.name: Alex Sarr
5160992:knee.note: Sarr (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Atlanta.
5160992:knee.long: Sarr is dealing with left knee soreness that could force him to miss another contest after sitting out Monday's win over Orlando. If the big man remains sidelined, Deandre Ayton could continue to handle an increased workload in Washington's frontcourt. Sarr's availability should become clearer closer to Wednesday's tipoff.

2581184:back.name: Anthony Gill
2581184:back.note: Gill (back) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
2581184:back.long: Gill's availability is uncertain as Washington deals with multiple injuries in its frontcourt. Gill's status should become clearer closer to tipoff, though he remains a limited fantasy option even if cleared to play.

5149077:suspension.name: Kingston Flemings
5149077:suspension.note: Flemings (suspension) won't play in Monday's game against Indiana, Andrew Schlecht of The Athletic reports.
5149077:suspension.long: Flemings was assessed a technical foul and ejected late in the Hawks' 121-99 loss to New Orleans on Saturday for intentionally elbowing Pelicans guard Bryce McGowens in the head. Without the rookie on the floor, head coach Quin Snyder will presumably divide the minutes between Dyson Daniels, Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Aaron Wiggins and CJ McCollum.

3936099:knee.name: Derrick Jones Jr.
3936099:knee.note: Jones (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
3936099:knee.long: Jones exited Sunday's loss to the Warriors and did not return due to a right knee injury. He's now listed on the injury report with right knee soreness, and the veteran forward's next chance to play will come Wednesday against Miami. In the meantime, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are candidates for increased playing time.

3134908:shoulder.name: Jakob Poeltl
3134908:shoulder.note: Poeltl (shoulder) is listed as probable for Friday's game against Milwaukee.
3134908:shoulder.long: Poeltl is still a little banged up for Toronto, but he intends to push through it. On Wednesday against Denver, he played 19 minutes off the bench with eight points, five rebounds and one assist.

4251:rest.name: Paul George
4251:rest.note: George will be rested Monday against Houston.
4251:rest.long: There's no injury to report and this appears to be a planned maintenance day for the veteran. With George on the shelf, the Celtics will need guys like Payton Pritchard and Baylor Scheierman to absorb more minutes.

4397040:quadriceps.name: Brandon Williams
4397040:quadriceps.note: Williams (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Suns.
4397040:quadriceps.long: Williams will be held out of the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quad contusion. His next chance to play will come Thursday against Miami. Will Richard and De'Anthony Melton could see a bump in minutes in Williams' stead.

3213:rest.name: Al Horford
3213:rest.note: Horford will be rested Monday against the Suns.
3213:rest.long: As expected, Horford will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set. Fortunately for the Warriors, Draymond Green (back) is set to return to the lineup.

2580365:illness.name: Larry Nance Jr.
2580365:illness.note: Nance (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Hawks.
2580365:illness.long: Including Nance, the Pacers have ruled out 10 players ahead of Monday's contest. Kobe Brown and Jarace Walker should see heavy workloads with the club shorthanded.

4396909:rest.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:rest.note: Nesmith (rest) is sitting out Monday against Atlanta.
4396909:rest.long: The Pacers are holding him out for left hamstring injury management, but this is a maintenance day and not a setback for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Kelly Oubre and Jarace Walker could see hefty workloads with so many Pacers sitting out.

4395712:neck.name: Andrew Nembhard
4395712:neck.note: Nembhard (cervical strain) is out for Monday's game against Atlanta.
4395712:neck.long: The Pacers are going to sit multiple key players for the second leg of this back-to-back set. With Nembhard sidelined, Quenton Jackson could be set up for an extended workload.

3149673:rest.name: Pascal Siakam
3149673:rest.note: Siakam will be rested against the Hawks on Monday.
3149673:rest.long: The veteran forward compiled 17 points (6-14 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 5-6 FT), five rebounds, five assists and a steal across 35 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 loss to the Nets, and he'll be held out for the second leg of this back-to-back set. Obi Toppin (lumbar sprain) is questionable, so the Pacers may need a lot of minutes from Jarace Walker.

4066648:quadriceps.name: Rui Hachimura
4066648:quadriceps.note: Hachimura (quadriceps) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Raptors.
4066648:quadriceps.long: The 28-year-old forward will miss the second leg of this back-to-back set due to a left quadriceps contusion, and his next chance to play will come Wednesday against the Heat. With Hachimura and Derrick Jones both sidelined, Kobe Sanders, Baba Miller and Gradey Dick are all candidates for increased playing time, especially if Max Strus (foot) operates under a minutes restriction in his regular-season debut with the Clippers.

4432847:hip.name: Terrence Shannon Jr.
4432847:hip.note: Shannon (hip) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
4432847:hip.long: Shannon's absence will leave Minnesota a bit shorthanded on the wing. His limited role makes the absence unlikely to have a significant fantasy impact, though the Timberwolves could distribute his available minutes among their remaining perimeter players.

4432816:wrist.name: LaMelo Ball
4432816:wrist.note: Ball is questionable for Monday's game against Milwaukee due to a right wrist contusion.
4432816:wrist.long: Ball's status is uncertain heading into Monday's matchup, leaving Minnesota's backcourt potentially shorthanded. With Anthony Edwards (knee) already ruled out, Ball's availability will be particularly important for the Timberwolves' offensive production. Bones Hyland and Ayo Dosunmu could be heavily involved if Ball is absent.

4712849:rest.name: Anthony Black
4712849:rest.note: Black will be rested Monday against the Wizards.
4712849:rest.long: The Magic are listing him out for left ankle injury management, so they are taking a cautious approach for the second leg of this back-to-back set. He finished with 23 points (6-12 FG, 1-5 3Pt, 10-11 FT), eight rebounds, three assists and two steals over 33 minutes Sunday against Boston. Jase Richardson, Jevon Carter and Jamal Cain could be more involved as a result.

4433134:hip.name: Scottie Barnes
4433134:hip.note: Barnes (hip) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Clippers.
4433134:hip.long: Barnes is dealing with left hip soreness and could miss the second leg of this back-to-back set. The star forward's absence would open up additional minutes for the likes of Collin Murray-Boyles, Jamison Battle and Allen Graves.

4432187:shoulder.name: Reece Beekman
4432187:shoulder.note: The Wizards announced Monday that Beekman sustained a right acromioclavicular joint injury and will be re-evaluated in approximately three weeks.
4432187:shoulder.long: Beekman is set for an extended absence, with his re-evaluation timeline suggesting he could remain sidelined beyond the initial three-week window. The injury further limits Washington's backcourt depth, though Beekman's absence is unlikely to have a significant impact on standard fantasy leagues.

4432582:hip.name: Max Christie
4432582:hip.note: Christie (hip) is probable for Friday's game against the Jazz.
4432582:hip.long: The swingman is primed to end a one-game absence Friday due to a hip injury. Christie had been starting at shooting guard for the Mavericks before getting hurt, but it remains to be seen if 2024 No. 1 overall pick Zaccharie Risacher has played well enough to keep his hold on a starting job.

3133603:knee.name: Kelly Oubre Jr.
3133603:knee.note: Oubre (knee) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Grizzlies.
3133603:knee.long: Oubre is trying to move past a knee contusion Wednesday. Less playing time would be available for Jarace Walker if Oubre is healthy enough to play.

4278355:coach-s-decision.name: Obi Toppin
4278355:coach-s-decision.note: Toppin (back) will dress for Monday's game against  Hawks but will only play in an emergency, Tony East of Forbes.com reports.
4278355:coach-s-decision.long: Toppin has missed the last two games while dealing with a lumbar strain, and the only reason he's dressing Monday is in the event of an emergency, as the Pacers are down to eight active players (including Toppin). Jay Huff, Kelly Oubre, Kobe Brown, Jarace Walker and Jalen Slawson will be tasked with eating up minutes in the frontcourt with Toppin, Ivica Zubac (ankle) and Larry Nance (illness) sidelined.

4278402:calf.name: Jordan Goodwin
4278402:calf.note: Goodwin (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Spurs, Kellan Olson of ArizonaSports.com reports.
4278402:calf.long: Goodwin will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a right calf injury, with his next chance to return coming Tuesday against the Clippers. Luke Kennard and Ryan Dunn are candidates for increased playing time in Goodwin's stead.

4066354:shoulder.name: Payton Pritchard
4066354:shoulder.note: Pritchard is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Milwaukee due to a right shoulder contusion, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4066354:shoulder.long: Pritchard's status is uncertain after he struggled in Monday's loss to Houston, finishing with four points on 0-for-7 shooting across 30 minutes. With Jayson Tatum (rest) also questionable and Devin Carter (illness) ruled out, Boston could be shorthanded Wednesday. Pritchard's availability should become clearer closer to tipoff.

4065648:rest.name: Jayson Tatum
4065648:rest.note: Tatum will be rested Wednesday against the Bucks, Jack Simone of BostonSportsJournal.com reports.
4065648:rest.long: The writing was on the wall for this one with the Celtics looking to get Tatum some planned rest. There's been no report of an injury, to be clear. Paul George, who is coming off a maintenance day himself, is in line for a big bump in usage Wednesday.

3062679:ankle.name: Josh Hart
3062679:ankle.note: Hart is doubtful for Tuesday's game against the Bucks due to an illness.
3062679:ankle.long: Hart is in line to miss a third straight contest, but it appears he's moved past ankle soreness that previously bothered him. Until Hart is ready to return to the court, Landry Shamet will likely continue to start for the Knicks.

4432823:back.name: Jaylin Williams
4432823:back.note: Williams (back) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Portland and remains out indefinitely.
4432823:back.long: Williams is slated to miss a fifth straight game and doesn't have a return timetable, so it's fair to consider him week-to-week. With Chet Holmgren (knee) also sidelined, the Thunder will rely on Isaiah Hartenstein and Aday Mara.

4277919:ankle.name: Mo Bamba
4277919:ankle.note: Bamba (ankle) participated in Wednesday's morning shootaround, per Shreyas Laddha of The Salt Lake Tribune.
4277919:ankle.long: Bamba is trending in a positive direction ahead of Wednesday's game in New Orleans. He can be tentatively placed on the right side of his questionable designation.

3138196:ankle.name: Cameron Johnson
3138196:ankle.note: Johnson (lower body injury management) is listed as probable for Wednesday's game against Toronto.
3138196:ankle.long: Johnson has already missed three games. However, it doesn't appear he will be sidelined Wednesday versus the Raptors. The 30-year-old veteran hasn't played well throughout the 2026-27 campaign, averaging a career-low 8.0 points along with 5.0 rebounds, 2.0 assists and 1.0 steals over 26.3 minutes per contest in three regular-season appearances.

4431772:quadriceps.name: Myron Gardner
4431772:quadriceps.note: Gardner (quadriceps) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Clippers.
4431772:quadriceps.long: Gardner is in danger of missing his fourth contest of the 2026-27 campaign. However, he has logged three minutes or less in his four regular-season games, so his absence wouldn't have much of an effect on the rotation.

3032977:wrist.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
3032977:wrist.note: Antetokounmpo (wrist) is probable for Friday's game against Cleveland.
3032977:wrist.long: The superstar forward appears on track to suit up Friday despite dealing with a wrist sprain. Barring any setbacks, Antetokounmpo should be able to handle a normal workload and will be aiming to extend his streak of double-doubles with at least 20 points and 10 rebounds to nine games.

5105977:ankle.name: Rasheer Fleming
5105977:ankle.note: Fleming (ankle) is questionable for Saturday's game against the Rockets.
5105977:ankle.long: Fleming missed the Suns' last game and could be in line to miss a second straight contest due to a sprained left ankle. His absence shouldn't carry a ton of fantasy appeal, as he's averaging just 0.5 points and 1.5 rebounds in two outings off the bench this season.

4431679:ankle.name: Precious Achiuwa
4431679:ankle.note: Achiuwa (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Trail Blazers.
4431679:ankle.long: Achiuwa is sitting out Friday for the first time this season due to left ankle soreness, and he can be deemed day-to-day going forward. His absence likely paves the way for Keegan Murray to re-enter the starting lineup after opening 2026-27 as the Kings' starting power forward.

4432170:groin.name: Isaiah Jackson
4432170:groin.note: Jackson (groin) won't suit up for Sunday's game against the Pelicans, Law Murray of The Athletic reports.
4432170:groin.long: Jackson played through the groin issue in Wednesday's 117-116 loss to the Heat, but logged a season-low 13 minutes, suggesting the injury was bothering him. For now, Jackson should be considered questionable for Tuesday's game in Phoenix. Baba Miller will serve as the backup center with Jackson sidelined Sunday.

4697268:ankle.name: Kam Jones
4697268:ankle.note: Jones (ankle/two-way player) is out for Friday's game against Toronto.
4697268:ankle.long: It's not clear whether Jones is still dealing with a right ankle injury, or if he's been ruled out due to his status as a two-way player. He'll presumably open the year with the G League's Wisconsin Herd once he's back at full strength.

4279318:illness.name: Daeqwon Plowden
4279318:illness.note: Plowden (illness) is out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
4279318:illness.long: Plowden is under the weather and can be considered day-to-day. Dylan Cardwell's (calf) season debut is coming at an opportune time for the Kings on Wednesday.

5104155:illness.name: Bilal Coulibaly
5104155:illness.note: Coulibaly (illness) is questionable for Wednesday against the Hawks.
5104155:illness.long: Coulibaly was a late addition to the injury report after waking up under the weather. If the Wizards end up holding Coulibaly out, the team could turn to Khris Middleton and/or Will Riley.

4873201:toe.name: Asa Newell
4873201:toe.note: Newell (toe) has been ruled out for Friday's game against Chicago.
4873201:toe.long: Newell will miss a fourth consecutive contest due to a left great toe hyperextension. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks provide an update on his progress.

4066354:eye.name: Payton Pritchard
4066354:eye.note: Pritchard (eye) is questionable for Friday against Charlotte, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4066354:eye.long: Pritchard is day-to-day after leaving Wednesday's win over the Bucks early. Meanwhile, Jayson Tatum (rest) has been cleared to return. Guys like Baylor Scheierman and Mike Conley could see more run if Pritchard is unable to give it a go.

4432194:undisclosed.name: Day'Ron Sharpe
4432194:undisclosed.note: Sharpe registered 15 points (5-7 FG, 1-1 3Pt, 4-5 FT), 13 rebounds and four assists across 26 minutes in Sunday's 98-90 win over the Pacers.
4432194:undisclosed.long: Sharpe dominated the glass, collecting four offensive rebounds while shooting efficiently en route to his first double-double of the season. It was also the second time he scored in double digits this season. Sharpe's rebounding provides a useful foundation, although his ceiling will depend on whether Brooklyn consistently gives him enough touches and playing time -- he has played more than 25 minutes just twice all season long.

4712896:knee.name: Noah Clowney
4712896:knee.note: Clowney (knee) supplied seven points (3-6 FG, 1-4 3Pt), one rebound and one assist over 17 minutes during Wednesday's 114-104 victory over the Hornets.
4712896:knee.long: Despite playing in all eight games thus far, Clowney has been mostly a non-factor for the Nets. In 21.0 minutes per game, Clowney has averaged just 5.6 points and 4.4 rebounds, barely making him a top 300 player. Outside of very deep leagues, there is no reason to pay any attention to Clowney.

5061575:leg.name: Kon Knueppel
5061575:leg.note: Knueppel exited Wednesday's game against the Nets after experiencing soreness in his left leg and he will not return, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
5061575:leg.long: This is the same leg that delayed Knueppel's season debut, but for now the team is calling it a leg injury rather than specifically citing his hamstring. Still, it's concerning that he seemingly suffered a non-contact injury after just six minutes of play. For now, Knueppel should be considered questionable for Friday's meeting with the Celtics.

4066650:undisclosed.name: Zach Collins
4066650:undisclosed.note: Collins (undisclosed) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks, finishing with three points (1-4 FG, 0-2 3Pt, 1-1 FT), three assists, one rebound and one steal across 14 minutes.
4066650:undisclosed.long: Collins headed back to the locker room with a trainer and did not return. He can be considered questionable for Sunday's game against the Sixers until the Bulls offer an update on his status. If the big man is forced to miss time, Leonard Miller could see increased burn.

4397189:hand.name: Jalen Smith
4397189:hand.note: Smith (hand) exited Friday's 125-117 win over the Hawks in overtime and did not return, finishing with 15 points (6-15 FG, 1-6 3Pt, 2-2 FT), 12 rebounds, three assists and three steals across 32 minutes.
4397189:hand.long: Smith secured his third double-double of the season while tying his season-high mark in steals. However, the big man came down on his left hand in overtime and exited to the locker room. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Saturday's game at Minnesota.

4066328:knee.name: Jarrett Allen
4066328:knee.note: Allen (knee) is questionable for Monday's game against Charlotte.
4066328:knee.long: Allen has missed the last two contests due to a bruised right knee. Sam Merrill (elbow) is also sidelined, so Meleek Thomas may remain in the starting lineup, with Peyton Watson sliding over to the four and Evan Mobley handling things at the five.

5023693:ankle.name: Tyrese Proctor
5023693:ankle.note: Proctor (ankle) is questionable to play in Friday's game against the 76ers.
5023693:ankle.long: Proctor sprained his left ankle in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 124-116 loss to the Thunder and did not return. The 22-year-old is one of several Cavaliers currently dealing with an injury, as Jaylon Tyson (ankle), Peyton Watson (hamstring) and Jarrett Allen (knee) are all banged up. Proctor's next chance to play comes Saturday against the Knicks on the second leg of Cleveland's back-to-back set.

3978:back.name: DeMar DeRozan
3978:back.note: DeRozan is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to lower back spasms.
3978:back.long: DeRozan missed Wednesday's game against the Raptors due to back spasms, which now has him questionable for Monday's contest. If he is unable to go, Alpha Diallo, Bryce Hopkins and Trevon Brazile are candidates for increased minutes.

3133603:calf.name: Kelly Oubre Jr.
3133603:calf.note: Oubre (calf) is questionable for Saturday's game against Denver.
3133603:calf.long: Oubre is trying to end a two-game absence Saturday due to a calf contusion. Less playing time would be open to Jarace Walker and Obi Toppin if Oubre is able to return.

4432810:knee.name: Isaiah Stewart
4432810:knee.note: Stewart (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game versus the Nuggets.
4432810:knee.long: Stewart has played well in his first season in Memphis, averaging a career-high 11.9 points while shooting 57.1 percent from downtown. He has missed the last two games due to a bone bruise in his right knee. If Stewart remains sidelined Wednesday, GG Jackson and Taylor Hendricks are candidates for more minutes.

5105637:head.name: Adem Bona
5105637:head.note: Bona exited Wednesday's 112-106 win over the Pistons in the fourth quarter and did not return due to an apparent head injury, finishing with five points (2-4 FG, 1-1 FT), two rebounds, one assist and one steal across 15 minutes.
5105637:head.long: Bona headed back to the locker room with trainers and never checked back in. The big man can be considered questionable ahead of Friday's game at Cleveland.

4578893:ankle.name: Vit Krejci
4578893:ankle.note: Krejci underwent surgery on his fractured left ankle Wednesday and will be re-evaluated in eight weeks, Brett Siegel of ClutchPoints.com reports.
4578893:ankle.long: Krejci suffered the ankle injury in last Wednesday's win over the Suns and is set to miss an extended period after undergoing surgery. With the 26-year-old and Ja Morant (hamstring) both on the shelf, Jrue Holiday and Sidy Cissoko should continue seeing increased minutes.

4585618:knee.name: Keshon Gilbert
4585618:knee.note: Gilbert (knee) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Bulls.
4585618:knee.long: Gilbert continues to deal with lingering knee inflammation and is without a timetable to return. He can be considered week-to-week until the Hawks offer an update on his progress.

3032979:thigh.name: Dennis Schroder
3032979:thigh.note: Schroder (thigh) is out for Friday's game versus Boston.
3032979:thigh.long: Schroder is sitting out Friday for the first time this season due to left thigh soreness. With the veteran floor general sidelined, Coby White should see his minutes climb into the 20s for the first time this year as he works back from a preseason calf strain.

4433249:quadriceps.name: Moussa Diabate
4433249:quadriceps.note: Diabate (quadriceps) is listed as probable for Thursday's game against the Suns.
4433249:quadriceps.long: Diabate is expected to return from a two-game absence Thursday, which would leave fewer minutes available for Ryan Kalkbrenner. Through nine regular-season games, Diabate has averaged 8.9 points, 9.1 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.6 steals and 0.9 blocks in 28.8 minutes per tilt.

5105637:back.name: Adem Bona
5105637:back.note: Bona (back) will be re-evaluated in approximately one week after seeing a specialist, Ky Carlin of USA Today reports.
5105637:back.long: The fact that Bona needed to see a specialist suggests the injury may be more significant than initially thought, and he'll remain sidelined for at least the next several games. Even when healthy, the big man has seen his role shrink with Joel Embiid (foot) back in the rotation, averaging just 0.7 points, 1.7 rebounds and 1.0 blocks in four appearances outside of his 25-minute effort against the Pistons in late October. In Bona's absence, Jabari Walker could see a few more minutes as Philadelphia's backup center.

6583:ankle.name: Anthony Davis
6583:ankle.note: Davis (ankle) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.
6583:ankle.long: Davis has missed the last two games. It appears he has a chance to return Monday against the Pistons. However, if Davis isn't cleared to suit up for that contest, Bilal Coulibaly could remain in the starting lineup. Deandre Ayton (leg), who is not listed on the injury report, is also a candidate to start.

4278580:illness.name: Sandro Mamukelashvili
4278580:illness.note: Mamukelashvili (illness) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Portland.
4278580:illness.long: Mamukelashvili is under the weather and could miss his first game of the season Friday. If the big man is unable to suit up, Jarred Vanderbilt and Jake LaRavia would be candidates to see increased minutes.

4433134:groin.name: Scottie Barnes
4433134:groin.note: Barnes (groin) is out for Thursday's game against Philadelphia.
4433134:groin.long: The star forward is missing a fourth straight game with a groin strain. Ja'Kobe Walter should continue to take on additional playmaking responsibilites in Barnes' stead, while Collin Murray-Boyles should keep starting at power forward.

2993874:illness.name: Kyle Anderson
2993874:illness.note: Anderson is questionable for Friday against the Bucks due to illness.
2993874:illness.long: Anderson is averaging 6.1 minutes across six appearances so far. His status won't carry much weight in fantasy hoops.

4066650:illness.name: Zach Collins
4066650:illness.note: Collins (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs.
4066650:illness.long: Collins is in danger of missing his second straight game due to an illness. If he's out again, Jalen Smith and Leonard Miller would likely split Collins' minutes.

6442:illness.name: Kyrie Irving
6442:illness.note: Irving (illness) is probable for Friday's game against Utah.
6442:illness.long: Irving presumably woke up Friday morning under the weather. The issue isn't expected to prevent the star guard from playing, and Irving is likely to go through pregame warmups before Dallas confirms his status.

6589:elbow.name: Draymond Green
6589:elbow.note: Green (elbow) is listed as questionable ahead of Saturday's game against Orlando.
6589:elbow.long: Green is coming off an 11-assist performance in Thursday's 120-100 win over the Heat. He's in danger of missing his third contest of the 2026-27 campaign due to elbow inflammation. If Green is downgraded to out, Charles Bassey and Al Horford would likely split time at the five.

3134903:calf.name: Gary Payton II
3134903:calf.note: Payton is questionable to play Saturday against the Magic due to right calf tightness.
3134903:calf.long: We'll have a better idea on Payton's status based on his activity level at Saturday's shootaround, but if he's forced to the sidelines, that would open up some minutes for Brandon Williams and De'Anthony Melton. LJ Cryer would also have the opportunity to get into the rotation sans Payton.

4065732:illness.name: De'Andre Hunter
4065732:illness.note: Hunter (illness) is listed as out for Friday's game against San Antonio.
4065732:illness.long: Hunter was listed as questionable but has now been ruled out for the first time this season. His next opportunity to play will come Sunday versus the Heat. Without Hunter, Malik Monk might find his way into the starting lineup.

4395724:hamstring.name: Immanuel Quickley
4395724:hamstring.note: Quickley (hamstring) is questionable for Wednesday's game against Boston.
4395724:hamstring.long: Quickley has a chance Wednesday to end a two-game absence with a hamstring injury. Jamal Shead would have the most to lose from a fantasy perspective if Quickley is able to return.

4433287:groin.name: Brandon Miller
4433287:groin.note: Miller (groin) is listed as out for Thursday's game against Phoenix.
4433287:groin.long: Miller injured his groin during the 119-80 loss to Boston on Friday and subsequently missed Monday's meeting with Cleveland. Now that Miller is confirmed to be sidelined for a second consecutive contest, Sion James is the favorite to remain in the starting lineup.

4066757:elbow.name: Sam Merrill
4066757:elbow.note: Merrill (elbow) is listed as out for Wednesday's game against the Knicks.
4066757:elbow.long: Merrill has battled a lingering elbow issue since the preseason. He will now miss a third consecutive contest, with his next opportunity to suit up coming Friday in Miami. While Merrill is sidelined, Craig Porter, Meleek Thomas and Tyrese Proctor should see more minutes.

5279133:fracture.name: Joan Beringer
5279133:fracture.note: Beringer (nose) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Jazz.
5279133:fracture.long: Beringer broke his nose during Friday's win over the Pelicans, so he might need to miss Sunday's game. If he's out, Trey Lyles would have the chance for some extended run.

4712896:illness.name: Noah Clowney
4712896:illness.note: Clowney is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against the Hawks due to an illness.
4712896:illness.long: Recently recovered from a knee injury, Clowney could now be at risk of sitting out Saturday's contest due to being under the weather. Josh Minott could pick up some extra playing time if Clowney is unable to play.

5105462:knee.name: Richie Saunders
5105462:knee.note: Saunders signed a two-way contract with the Grizzlies on Saturday, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5105462:knee.long: Saunders is still on the mend from a torn right ACL that he suffered during his final year at BYU. However, he has been cleared for on-court activities and will be allowed to practice with the Grizzlies now that he's officially signed with the team.

5105555:knee.name: Tobe Awaka
5105555:knee.note: Awaka (knee) is questionable for Sundays' game against the 76ers.
5105555:knee.long: Awaka missed Wednesday's 135-105 loss to the Knicks due to a sprained left MCL, and he's now in danger of missing a second consecutive outing with the ailment. Zach Collins (illness) has already been ruled out Sunday, leaving Noa Essengue, Leonard Miller and Patrick Williams as candidates to see more opportunities off Chicago's bench.

5107818:not-injury-related.name: Isaac Jones
5107818:not-injury-related.note: Jones posted 18 points (6-14 FG, 0-3 3Pt, 3-3 FT), 10 rebounds, an assist, two steals and two blocks in Wednesday's 100-88 Summer League loss to the Suns.
5107818:not-injury-related.long: Jones was one of four Phoenix players who scored at least 15 points, and he also led the team in rebounds and blocks while ranking second in steals. This was Jones' second double-double in four Summer League contests, and the third time he has surpassed the 15-point threshold.

4397449:not-injury-related.name: Elijah Harkless
4397449:not-injury-related.note: Harkless signed a two-way contract with the Pistons, Keith Smith of Spotrac.com reports.
4397449:not-injury-related.long: Harkless is no longer a free agent after the Jazz declined his team option back in June. A defensive-minded wing, Harkless will likely play a prominent role for Detroit's G League affiliate in the early going.

3945274:back.name: Luka Doncic
3945274:back.note: Doncic has been ruled out for Sunday's game at Detroit due to lower-back tightness, Trevor Lane of LakersNation.com reports.
3945274:back.long: Doncic will be held out of the front end of this back-to-back set, with his next chance to suit up coming Monday at Atlanta. With the superstar floor general sidelined, Austin Reaves will likely see increased scoring and playmaking duties, while Quentin Grimes and Collin Sexton could see an uptick in minutes.

4066320:illness.name: Desmond Bane
4066320:illness.note: Bane (illness) has been ruled out for Saturday's game against the Warriors.
4066320:illness.long: Bane will miss Saturday night's contest in Golden State with an illness. He joins Paolo Banchero (ankle) and Jalen Suggs (knee) on the sidelines, as the Magic now have 60 percent of their opening night starting lineup donning street clothes. Bane's next chance to suit up will come Tuesday versus the Kings. In his absence, expect Jase Richardson, Jamal Cain and Jevon Carter to absorb extra minutes.

4066211:rest.name: Robert Williams III
4066211:rest.note: Williams (rest) won't play in Saturday's game against the Spurs.
