4066211:rest.long: Williams logged 16 minutes in Friday's 124-118 loss to the Lakers, though he won't play Saturday versus San Antonio, the second game of a back-to-back for Portland. As a result, Branden Carlson and Yang Hansen should each receive more playing time behind Donovan Clingan.

4066336:wrist.name: Lauri Markkanen
4066336:wrist.note: Markkanen is out for Tuesday's game versus the Heat with a right wrist sprain.
4066336:wrist.long: The star forward is missing a second consecutive contest, and he faces a short turnaround to return ahead of Wednesday's tilt against the Magic. Josh Green figures to draw a second straight start, while Brice Sensabaugh and Josh Okogie should see a bump in playing time.

4278129:leg.name: Deandre Ayton
4278129:leg.note: Ayton won't return to Saturday's game against the Thunder due to a lower leg injury.
4278129:leg.long: Ayton will end his evening with two points (1-2 FG), one rebound and one turnover in seven minutes. For now, he should be considered questionable for Monday's game in Detroit.

4702670:knee.name: Grant Nelson
4702670:knee.note: Nelson signed a two-way contract with the Nets on Friday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
4702670:knee.long: Nelson appeared in four regular-season games for the Nets during the 2025-26 campaign and will link up with the franchise again. He's expected to spend the bulk of his time with their G League affiliate to open the season.

2595516:shoulder.name: Norman Powell
2595516:shoulder.note: Powell (shoulder) is questionable for Friday's game against the Hawks.
2595516:shoulder.long: Powell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence due to a shoulder injury. With rookie standout Caleb Wilson (hand) going on the shelf for multiple weeks, Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro both have a chance to step up for the Bulls.

4433627:illness.name: Keyonte George
4433627:illness.note: George (illness) has been downgraded to questionable for Sunday's game against Minnesota.
4433627:illness.long: George presumably woke up under the weather before being a late addition to the injury report. If the star point guard is unable to suit up, Darryn Peterson could see additional on-ball duties. Additionally, Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk would be candidates for increased playing time.

4351852:illness.name: Mitchell Robinson
4351852:illness.note: Robinson (illness) is questionable for Sunday's game versus Milwaukee, Bobby Krivitsky of Forbes.com reports.
4351852:illness.long: Robinson isn't feeling well, so he may not be available against the Bucks, which would mark his second absence of the 2026-27 campaign. If Robinson can't suit up, it should mean more minutes for Luka Garza behind Neemias Queta.

4277843:illness.name: Gary Trent Jr.
4277843:illness.note: Trent (illness) won't play in Sunday's game versus the Celtics.
4277843:illness.long: Trent will miss his fourth consecutive game Sunday. However, since he has totaled only 13 minutes in his two appearances this season, his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

3032979:hamstring.name: Dennis Schroder
3032979:hamstring.note: Schroder has been diagnosed with a left hamstring strain and will be reevaluated in two weeks, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
3032979:hamstring.long: Schroder, who missed Friday's game due to what was described as a left thigh injury, has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain. He is set to be reevaluated in two weeks, suggesting he will miss at least the next five games. Christian Anderson and Sion James could see extra minutes with Schroder sidelined.

3138196:lower-body.name: Cameron Johnson
3138196:lower-body.note: Johnson (lower body) is questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
3138196:lower-body.long: Johnson has already missed three games this season. If he is unavailable for a fourth time Monday versus the Rockets, it could mean more minutes for Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo.

4431767:calf.name: Christian Braun
4431767:calf.note: Braun (calf/illness) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against Houston.
4431767:calf.long: Braun is under the weather and also dealing with a left calf contusion. Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Aaron Gordon (lower body), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back) are all listed as questionable as well, so the Nuggets could be shorthanded Monday. If Braun is ruled out, Spencer Jones, Cam Whitmore and Bryce Hopkins would be candidates for increased minutes.

3936299:lower-leg.name: Jamal Murray
3936299:lower-leg.note: Murray is questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets due to a left shin contusion.
3936299:lower-leg.long: Murray could miss his first game of the season due to a right lower leg injury. If he is unavailable, Tyus Jones could see an expanded role.

3064290:lower-body.name: Aaron Gordon
3064290:lower-body.note: Gordon (lower body injury management) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against the Rockets.
3064290:lower-body.long: Along with Nikola Jokic (elbow), Jamal Murray (shin), Christian Braun (calf/illness), Cameron Johnson (lower body) and DeMar DeRozan (back), Gordon is questionable to play Monday. If the veteran forward is unable to go, Trevon Brazile, Spencer Jones and Alpha Diallo would be candidates for increased playing time.

3112335:elbow.name: Nikola Jokic
3112335:elbow.note: Jokic (elbow) is listed as questionable for Monday's game in Houston.
3112335:elbow.long: Jokic nearly had a triple-double in Saturday's 114-102 win over the Pacers. However, he's now in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 season due to a right elbow sprain. If Jokic isn't available to suit up, Marvin Bagley would presumably take his place in the starting lineup.

4897262:thumb.name: Will Richard
4897262:thumb.note: Richard (thumb) has been upgraded to probable for Wednesday's game at Houston.
4897262:thumb.long: Richard is expected to play through a torn UCL in his left thumb. Over his last five games (two starts), the 23-year-old has averaged 5.2 points, 2.0 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 18.2 minutes per tilt.

4397014:finger.name: Quentin Grimes
4397014:finger.note: Grimes (finger) said he expects to return to action Sunday against the Suns, according to Ricardo Sandoval of Lakers on SI.
4397014:finger.long: Grimes has missed the Lakers' last two games, but it sounds as if he could return to the rotation Sunday. It's unclear whether he'd be a starter, but he'd have a chance if Austin Reaves (heel) isn't cleared. Grimes is averaging 8.0 points per game this season, but that number rises to 17.5 points per game in his two starts.

3155942:knee.name: Domantas Sabonis
3155942:knee.note: Sabonis (knee) is questionable to play Tuesday's game against the Magic.
3155942:knee.long: Sabonis missed Sunday's 114-108 loss to the Heat with left knee soreness, making it his first absence of the season through 10 games. Dylan Cardwell earned the start with Sabonis sidelined, so if the latter is forced to miss a second straight contest, the former would be the top candidate to start once again.

4395630:groin.name: Devin Vassell
4395630:groin.note: Vassell is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left adductor tightness.
4395630:groin.long: Vassell is trying to avoid a third consecutive absence with the issue. Julian Champagnie would likely draw a third straight start at power forward for the Spurs on Friday if Vassell is unable to play.

4433627:ankle.name: Keyonte George
4433627:ankle.note: George (ankle) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Heat.
4433627:ankle.long: George sustained a right ankle sprain in Sunday's loss to Minnesota and will be sidelined for the front end of this back-to-back set. His next opportunity to play will come Wednesday against Orlando, and the 23-year-old's absence should open up additional minutes for guys like Isaiah Collier and Svi Mykhailiuk. Moreover, Darryn Peterson figures to take on additional on-ball duties.

4873153:leg.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
4873153:leg.note: Johnson (leg) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Pacers.
4873153:leg.long: Johnson will miss his first game of the 2026-27 campaign after tallying four points, nine rebounds and one assist in 19 minutes in the first half of a back-to-back set Sunday against Brooklyn. His absence could open up more minutes for Santi Aldama and Moussa Cisse behind starting center Daniel Gafford.

3134903:knee.name: Gary Payton II
3134903:knee.note: Payton (knee) is out for Wednesday's game against Houston.
3134903:knee.long: Payton is sidelined for a second consecutive contest with knee inflammation. Will Richard (thumb) could slot into Payton's spot in the backcourt rotation Wednesday.

4397040:hamstring.name: Brandon Williams
4397040:hamstring.note: Williams (hamstring) will miss at least one week, per Anthony Slater of ESPN.com.
4397040:hamstring.long: Williams has been diagnosed with a hamstring strain in the aftermath of Monday's game against the Pelicans, and his status for Golden State's upcoming five-game road trip is in serious doubt. With Williams facing an extended absence, the Warriors are likely to lean more on De'Anthony Melton in the backourt.

4432827:illness.name: Oscar Tshiebwe
4432827:illness.note: Tshiebwe has been ruled out for Monday's game against the Nuggets due to an illness.
4432827:illness.long: With Clint Capela (ankle) and Steven Adams (calf) sidelined, Tshiebwe has been able to appear in six straight games, averaging 6.8 minutes a night. With all three backup centers unavailable, Jabari Smith and Tari Eason might play some small-ball five minutes behind Alperen Sengun.

4845363:ankle.name: Cam Christie
4845363:ankle.note: Christie (ankle) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Phoenix.
4845363:ankle.long: Christie will miss his fifth game of the 2026-27 campaign. The 21-year-old rookie has averaged only 6.0 minutes per contest in his five regular-season appearances, so his absence won't have much of an effect on the rotation.

4066457:illness.name: Austin Reaves
4066457:illness.note: Reaves (illness) has been ruled out for Monday's game against Atlanta, Benjamin Royer of The Orange County Register reports.
4066457:illness.long: Reaves was added to the injury report earlier in the day after being diagnosed with an illness, and he's since been downgraded to out. This will mark his first absence of the 2026-27 campaign, presumably opening up opportunities for Collin Sexton and Cameron Carr.

4593016:head.name: Quinten Post
4593016:head.note: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Nuggets.
4593016:head.long: Post suffered a concussion during Monday's 118-102 win over the Raptors, and now he will have to clear a series of steps before he's allowed to return to the court. Taylor Hendricks will help pick up the slack while Post is sidelined.

4395725:knee.name: Tyler Herro
4395725:knee.note: Herro (knee) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against the Lakers.
4395725:knee.long: Herro is in jeopardy of missing a second consecutive contest due to a right knee contusion. If the star guard remains on the inactive list, Ryan Rollins would likely stay in the starting five, while Kasparas Jakucionis could continue seeing increased burn off the bench.

4431675:ankle.name: Trendon Watford
4431675:ankle.note: Watford (ankle) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
4431675:ankle.long: Friday marks a third consecutive absence for Watford, who has no timetable for a return with a sprained ankle. His absence solidifies DeAndre Jordan's spot in the center rotation.

4395628:rest.name: Zion Williamson
4395628:rest.note: Williamson (rest) is out for Monday's game against the Warriors.
4395628:rest.long: The Pelicans are giving the star forward a maintenance day on the second half of this back-to-back, but Williamson should be able to play Wednesday against the Nets. With Trey Murphy (knees) also sidelined, Derik Queen, Saddiq Bey and Herbert Jones stand out as the most likely candidates to enter the starting lineup Monday.

4594327:wrist.name: Keegan Murray
4594327:wrist.note: Murray is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Magic due to right wrist soreness.
4594327:wrist.long: Murray made his return to court Sunday against Miami following a seven-game absence due to an ankle injury, and it now appears he's dealing with a wrist issue. The Kings will presumably monitor him closely during shootaround and warmups to determine if he can suit up Tuesday.

5093267:illness.name: Collin Murray-Boyles
5093267:illness.note: Murray-Boyles (illness) is questionable for Wednesday's game against the Celtics.
5093267:illness.long: The Raptors are likely to check back in with Murray-Boyles closer to Wednesday's tipoff. Jamison Battle would handle an expanded role in the frontcourt if Murray-Boyles ends up sitting out.

5104155:hand.name: Bilal Coulibaly
5104155:hand.note: Coulibaly (hand) is out for Monday's game against the Pistons.
5104155:hand.long: Coulibaly is missing his first game of the season Monday with a hand injury. Tre Johnson and Bub Carrington both make sense as streaming options for fantasy managers in the short term.

5105623:ankle.name: Kel'el Ware
5105623:ankle.note: Ware is questionable for Tuesday's game against the Knicks due to a left ankle sprain.
5105623:ankle.long: Ware was a late addition to the injury report, which is never a good sign, but the severity of the issue remains unclear. If the backup big man is unable to suit up, Jericho Sims, Nate Ament and Ousmane Dieng would be candidates for increased roles.

4702382:calf.name: Tristan da Silva
4702382:calf.note: Da Silva (calf) participated in Friday's morning shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against Milwaukee, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
4702382:calf.long: Da Silva has already missed multiple games due to the calf issue, but this is a step in the right direction. His participation in shootaround is a positive sign, but he'll still need to be cleared before Orlando can count on him for frontcourt minutes against the Bucks.

5279130:calf.name: Nolan Traore
5279130:calf.note: Traore (calf) is listed as probable for Saturday's game against Memphis.
5279130:calf.long: Traore appears on track to suit up despite dealing with discomfort in his right calf. The guard's expected availability should help Brooklyn maintain its backcourt depth, though his fantasy appeal remains dependent on his playing time and opportunities in the rotation. His status should be confirmed ahead of Saturday's tipoff.

5105555:back.name: Tobe Awaka
5105555:back.note: Awaka (back) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Hawks.
5105555:back.long: Awaka will miss a second consecutive contest due to a back issue. His next chance to suit up will come Saturday at Minnesota.

3062679:illness.name: Josh Hart
3062679:illness.note: Hart (illness) is probable for Wednesday's game against the Cavaliers.
3062679:illness.long: Hart has missed three games in a row. First, he was sidelined for two contests due to a knee injury but didn't play Tuesday against the Bucks due to an illness. It appears he's moved past both issues and will return to action Wednesday. However, the veteran wing has been off to a slow start this season, averaging 8.6 points, 7.3 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 2.1 steals in 31.6 minutes per game.

4431684:illness.name: Trayce Jackson-Davis
4431684:illness.note: Jackson-Davis is out for Thursday's game against the 76ers due to an illness.
4431684:illness.long: Jackson-Davis is missing both ends of Toronto's back-to-back set with the ailment. Jamison Battle should handle a larger role in the frontcourt Thursday.

4431679:lower-leg.name: Precious Achiuwa
4431679:lower-leg.note: Achiuwa left Tuesday's 107-100 loss to the Magic with a left lower leg contusion and did not return, Matt George of ABC 10 Sacramento reports.
4431679:lower-leg.long: With Achiuwa exiting the game after 14 minutes, more minutes became available for Dylan Cardwell. If Achiuwa needs to miss Friday's game against the Trail Blazers, Keegan Murray would likely return to the starting lineup, and Cardwell would have the chance for some extended run.

4251:illness.name: Paul George
4251:illness.note: George (illness) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Toronto, Taylor Snow of the Celtics' official site reports.
4251:illness.long: George will sit out the second leg of this back-to-back set due to an illness, and his next opportunity to play will come Sunday against the Mavericks. With the veteran forward sidelined, Baylor Scheierman, Sam Hauser and Hugo Gonzalez are all candidates to see increased playing time.

5101761:illness.name: Mikel Brown Jr.
5101761:illness.note: Brown (illness) is listed as questionable for Saturday's game against Memphis.
5101761:illness.long: Brown is under the weather and could miss a third consecutive contest. If the rookie guard is unable to suit up, Egor Demin, Keon Ellis and Nolan Traore (calf), who is listed as probable, would be candidates for increased playing time.

5095151:hip.name: Caleb Wilson
5095151:hip.note: Wilson has been downgraded to questionable for Wednesday's game against the Spurs due to right hip soreness.
5095151:hip.long: Wilson was a late addition to the injury report and will likely be a game-time decision ahead of tipoff at 8:00 p.m. ET. If the rookie forward isn't cleared to play, Leonard Miller and Noa Essengue would likely see increased playing time.

5037878:foot.name: Ugonna Onyenso
5037878:foot.note: Onyenso agreed to a two-way contract with the Pistons on Thursday.
5037878:foot.long: The No. 53 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft, Onyenso appears poised to see run in the G League after putting pen to paper on a two-way deal. He'll likely face an uphill battle to carve out a role in the rotation, so Detroit will presumably allow him to continue his development with Motor City.

3133628:rest.name: Myles Turner
3133628:rest.note: Turner has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Lakers due to rest.
3133628:rest.long: Turner will miss his first game of the season after totaling only three points in 27 minutes during Tuesday's blowout loss in New York. In Turner's absence, Kel'el Ware and Jericho Sims are candidates for increased roles. Turner should return to action Friday in Orlando.

4683634:thumb.name: Bennedict Mathurin
4683634:thumb.note: Mathurin (thumb) is listed as questionable for Friday's game against Memphis.
4683634:thumb.long: Mathurin now has a better chance of suiting up after being listed as doubtful. The Pelicans are likely to re-evaluate the swingman closer to Friday's tipoff, but his status may not have a major impact on the rotation.

3136195:calf.name: Karl-Anthony Towns
3136195:calf.note: Towns (calf) is listed as questionable for Wednesday's game against Cleveland.
3136195:calf.long: Towns may be held out of the second half of this back-to-back set due to a sore left calf. If the star big man is unable to play, Andre Drummond, Mohamed Diawara and James Wiseman would be candidates for increased playing time.

4066336:hand.name: Lauri Markkanen
4066336:hand.note: Markkanen has been diagnosed with a non-displaced fracture in his right hand and will be sidelined for at least one month, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
4066336:hand.long: Markkanen has missed two straight games due to what was being described as a right wrist sprain, but it appears the issue was much worse than initially thought. The talented big man now joins Jusuf Nurkic (foot) and Jaren Jackson (knee) on Utah's long-term injury list, while Keyonte George's status moving forward is unclear while dealing with an ankle sprain. Given all of the injuries, Ace Bailey and Darryn Peterson will have to lead the offense, while Isaiah Collier, Brice Sensabaugh, Svi Mykhailiuk, Josh Okogie and Josh Green are candidates for increased roles.

4873153:lower-leg.name: Morez Johnson Jr.
4873153:lower-leg.note: Johnson (left shin contusion) is listed as probable for Saturday against Cleveland.
4873153:lower-leg.long: Johnson appears to be trending toward availability after recently missing one game due to the shin injury. The rookie has averaged 6.9 points and 4.8 rebounds in 16.7 minutes per game this season, limiting his appeal to deeper fantasy formats.

4396909:knee.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:knee.note: Nesmith (knee) is questionable for Friday's game against the Knicks.
4396909:knee.long: Nesmith picked up a knee injury during Wednesday's game against Washington, and he was ultimately unable to return after being diagnosed with knee soreness. He'll likely test his knee during shootaround and pregame to determine if he can take the court Friday.

4900671:ankle.name: Ajay Mitchell
4900671:ankle.note: Mitchell (ankle) has been ruled out for Friday's game against the Clippers.
4900671:ankle.long: Mitchell will miss a second consecutive contest due to a let ankle sprain, and his next chance to play will come Sunday at Sacramento. With the 24-year-old guard out, Jared McCain, Bennett Stirtz and Nique Clifford are candidates for increased playing time.

4278572:shoulder.name: Jamal Cain
4278572:shoulder.note: Cain (shoulder) participated in Friday morning's shootaround and remains questionable for Friday's game against the Bucks, Jason Beede of the Orlando Sentinel reports.
4278572:shoulder.long: With Cain still carrying a questionable tag after shootaround and his availability still unsettled heading into Friday, his participation in morning practice is a step in the right direction. Cain is averaging 7.0 points on 19.5 minutes per game this season.

4706557:foot.name: Chris Youngblood
4706557:foot.note: Youngblood (foot) is out for Friday's game against Sacramento.
4706557:foot.long: Youngblood is in line for a second straight absence due to a bone bruise in his right foot. His next opportunity to run the floor will arrive Monday in Minnesota.

5095151:hand.name: Caleb Wilson
5095151:hand.note: Wilson (hand) is expected to miss four to six weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
5095151:hand.long: The rookie forward went down during Wednesday's loss to the Spurs, and he now needs surgery to repair a fractured right hand. More pressure will likely fall on Josh Giddey going forward, while the likes of Tre Jones and Isaac Okoro will have a chance for added streaming value.

3975:abdomen.name: Stephen Curry
3975:abdomen.note: Curry has been diagnosed with an oblique abdominal tear and will be re-evaluated in two weeks, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
3975:abdomen.long: Curry suffered the injury early during Wednesday's loss to the Rockets, with head coach Steve Kerr saying after the game that the superstar point guard "tweaked" something in his abdominal area. Curry has never dealt with an injury of this nature, so the Warriors, who are off to a hot start spearheaded by Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, will likely proceed with caution. Brandin Podziemski, Brandon Williams (hamstring), De'Anthony Melton, Will Richard and Gary Payton (knee) are all candidates for increased roles until Curry is cleared to play again.

4277811:head.name: Collin Sexton
4277811:head.note: Sexton did not return to Wednesday's 123-112 win over the Bucks and required stitches to close a cut on his forehead, Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times reports.
4277811:head.long: Sexton knocked noggins with Ryan Rollins, but it sounds like he's avoided a concussion, so he should be able to get out there for Sunday's game in Phoenix. Austin Reaves (heel) also exited Wednesday's game, and if he needs to sit out Sunday, Sexton would have the chance for some extended minutes.

4066457:heel.name: Austin Reaves
4066457:heel.note: Reaves (heel) won't undergo imaging and is considered day-to-day ahead of Sunday's game against the Suns, Jovan Buha of The Athletic reports.
4066457:heel.long: An official designation for Reaves' status will be given Saturday, according to Buha, and head coach JJ Redick also said Reaves has a bruise on his heel. The star guard is enjoying an excellent start to the season and is averaging 24.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals per game. If he's sidelined, expect Ziaire Williams to start in the backcourt alongside Luka Doncic.

3945274:ankle.name: Luka Doncic
3945274:ankle.note: Head coach JJ Redick said Friday that Doncic (ankle) is "fine," per Law Murray of The Athletic.
3945274:ankle.long: The superstar guard exited to the locker room late in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's win over the Bucks due to an apparent right ankle injury and did not return. Doncic can be tentatively placed on the right side of the questionable marker until the Lakers release an official injury report at some point prior to Sunday's matchup in Phoenix.

4591725:head.name: Ryan Rollins
4591725:head.note: Rollins (head) exited to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Wednesday's 123-112 loss to the Lakers and did not return, finishing with eight points (3-10 FG, 2-6 3Pt), seven rebounds, four assists and one steal across 24 minutes.
4591725:head.long: Rollins bumped heads with Collin Sexton with 6:51 remaining in the contest, and both players exited to the locker room. Rollins' status will be worth monitoring ahead of Friday's game at Orlando. If he needs to miss time, AJ Green and Kasparas Jakucionis could see increased playing time.

4601025:illness.name: Pelle Larsson
4601025:illness.note: Larsson (illness) is out for Friday's game against Cleveland.
4601025:illness.long: Larsson is sidelined for the first half of this back-to-back set with an illness. The expectation is that Andrew Wiggins will move back into the starting lineup after beginning the campaign as a member of the first unit.

6475:ankle.name: Klay Thompson
6475:ankle.note: Thompson (ankle) is out for Friday's game against the Cavaliers.
6475:ankle.long: The Heat sent mixed signals regarding the status of Thompson, first listing him as probable and later questionable before ruling him out altogether. With Andrew Wiggins already in line to fill in for Pelle Larsson (illness) on Friday, rookie second-rounder Ryan Conwell could be preparing for his first career start.

4433268:ankle.name: Trey Alexander
4433268:ankle.note: Alexander won't play Wednesday against the Grizzlies due to a left knee bone bruise.
4433268:ankle.long: Alexander sat out Friday's preseason finale with what the team initially described as a left knee injury, but we now know he's dealing with a bone bruise. Don't be surprised if Alexander misses Friday's game against the Pelicans as well.

5149077:back.name: Kingston Flemings
5149077:back.note: Flemings (back tightness) will not return to Friday's game against the Bulls.
5149077:back.long: Flemings carried a questionable tag into this game, and it appears as though he irritated his injury again. He ended up finishing scoreless with one rebound and one assist in 17 minutes. Consider him questionable for Sunday against the Bucks.

4432158:toe.name: Evan Mobley
4432158:toe.note: Mobley (toe) is out for Friday's game against the Heat.
4432158:toe.long: The star big man took a hard fall late in Wednesday's win over the Knicks, and he's missing his first contest of the season Friday with a sprained toe. With Mobley sidelined, Jaylon Tyson, Meleek Thomas and Mario Hezonja are each viable streaming options.

4397886:toe.name: Charles Bassey
4397886:toe.note: Bassey is probable for Friday's game against the Spurs due to left toe soreness.
4397886:toe.long: It's not clear as to when this injury popped up for Bassey, who missed the first two games of the season with a knee issue but has been otherwise healthy. Expect the team to confirm his availability for Friday as tipoff nears.

2990992:suspension.name: Marcus Smart
2990992:suspension.note: Smart has been suspended three games for throwing a punch during Wednesday's matchup against Golden State, Shams Charania of ESPN reports.
2990992:suspension.long: Smart, who was ejected from Wednesday's game for punching Charles Bassey, will begin serving his suspension Friday night against the Jazz, meaning he'll be eligible to return Wednesday versus Indiana. Bruce Thornton and Reed Sheppard should be in line for more minutes while Smart serves his three-game ban.

4593016:concussion.name: Quinten Post
4593016:concussion.note: Post (concussion) has been ruled out for Friday's game against New Orleans.
4593016:concussion.long: Post will miss a second straight game while in the league's concussion protocol, and his next opportunity to play will come Saturday against Brooklyn. With Zach Edey (left ankle injury management) sitting out the front end of this back-to-back set, Isaiah Stewart will likely get the starting nod, while Taylor Hendricks figures to see increased burn off the bench.

4600663:ankle.name: Zach Edey
4600663:ankle.note: Edey won't play in Friday's game against the Pelicans due to left ankle injury management.
4600663:ankle.long: Edey will get the night off after appearing in eight straight games for the Grizzlies. Isaiah Stewart and Taylor Hendricks are next in line for minutes at center considering both Edey and Quinten Post (concussion) are listed out for Friday.

4576086:elbow.name: Bryce McGowens
4576086:elbow.note: McGowens (elbow) is listed as out for Friday's game against the Grizzlies.
4576086:elbow.long: McGowens has been downgraded from doubtful to out with a left elbow infection. He faces a quick turnaround to return ahead of Saturday's tilt against Denver.

4066259:hip.name: De'Aaron Fox
4066259:hip.note: Fox is questionable for Friday's game against the Warriors due to left hip soreness.
4066259:hip.long: Fox is in danger of missing his first game of the 2026-27 season after picking up a hip injury. He'll presumably be re-evaluated again at some point before tipoff to determine his availability for Friday. Jordan McLaughlin and Julian Champagnie could see more minutes if Fox is unable to suit up.

4845374:chest.name: Bub Carrington
4845374:chest.note: Carrington (chest) has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game against the Pistons.
4845374:chest.long: Carrington played 16 minutes before exiting the contest due to a chest contusion. He had two points (1-6 FG, 0-3 3Pt) and two assists before being ruled out. Washington will provide an injury update when available.

3907497:ankle.name: Dejounte Murray
3907497:ankle.note: Murray (ankle) is out for Friday's game against Memphis.
3907497:ankle.long: This was the expectation after the star guard requested a trade from the Pelicans earlier Friday. Given his standing with the club, Murray can be tentatively considered doubtful for future contests while New Orleans tries to find him another home.

4431695:hand.name: Drew Timme
4431695:hand.note: The Suns claimed Timme off waivers Monday, per Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com.
4431695:hand.long: After being let go by Minnesota on Saturday, Timme wasn't allowed to go through waivers unclaimed without Phoenix snatching him up. With Mark Williams (shoulder) likely out through the All-Star break, Timme helps reinforce Phoenix's depth at center.

4411057:illness.name: Kevin McCullar Jr.
4411057:illness.note: McCullar signed a two-way contract with the Raptors on Thursday, Michael Scotto of HoopsHype.com reports.
4411057:illness.long: McCullar quickly finds a new home after being waived by the Knicks in late October. The forward is expected to play a prominent role for Toronto's G League affiliate.

5106268:back.name: Nae'Qwan Tomlin
5106268:back.note: Tomlin is set to miss several weeks with a lower back stress reaction, Chris Fedor of The Cleveland Plain Dealer reports.
5106268:back.long: This is a tough blow for the forward and there's no guarantee he's cleared right away when he's re-evaluated in three-to-four weeks. Tomlin wasn't projected to crack the rotation ahead of Opening Night and was penciled in to be an emergency depth option.

4432582:ankle.name: Max Christie
4432582:ankle.note: Christie is questionable for Saturday's game against the Cavaliers due to a sprained left ankle.
4432582:ankle.long: Christie is at risk of missing the front end of this back-to-back set with a lingering injury. His absence would result in an uptick in playing time for Zaccharie Risacher and Naji Marshall, which would bolster both players' streaming appeal.

4396909:hand.name: Aaron Nesmith
4396909:hand.note: Nesmith exited to the locker room in the final seconds of Friday's 106-104 win over the Knicks due to an apparent hand/wrist injury, Tony East of Forbes.com reports. He posted 18 points (7-10 FG, 2-3 3Pt, 2-2 FT), seven rebounds and one assist in 33 minutes.
4396909:hand.long: Nesmith turned in an extremely efficient performance and finished as Indiana's second-leading scorer. He was also second on the club in rebounds. However, the swingman's status will be worth monitoring ahead of Sunday's game at Philadelphia after he exited Friday's win early.

4397077:knee.name: Jaxson Hayes
4397077:knee.note: Hayes won't return to Friday's game against the Rockets due to a left knee issue.
4397077:knee.long: Hayes will end up missing the entire second half. He was playing well prior to the injury, finishing with 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting with five rebounds and one assist in 13 minutes. Mo Bamba could be in line for more run with this news.

5209602:coach-s-decision.name: Matilde Villa
5209602:coach-s-decision.note: Villa (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against New York.
5209602:coach-s-decision.long: Villa signed with Atlanta on Sept. 15 but will end the campaign without having seen any game action. She's ineligible to play in the postseason while on a developmental pact.

3058895:leg.name: Brionna Jones
3058895:leg.note: Jones will miss the remainder of the season after sustaining a left leg injury against the Sun on Aug. 13, Annie Costabile of The Athletic reports.
3058895:leg.long: This is a tough blow for a Dream team that is sitting in second place in the Eastern Conference. Jones managed to play in just nine games this campaign, finishing with averages of 8.2 points, 5.6 rebounds and 2.0 assists. Look for the Dream to use a committee approach to soak up those minutes going forward.

4066548:foot.name: DiJonai Carrington
4066548:foot.note: Carrington (foot) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
4066548:foot.long: Carrington will end the season on the inactive list for a fifth consecutive contest due to a left foot injury. She'll finish the campaign having averaged 8.8 points, 3.1 rebounds, 0.6 assists and 0.6 steals in 16.2 minutes per game across 11 regular-season outings. She's set to enter unrestricted free agency this offseason following an injury-riddled year.

4433433:knee.name: Aicha Coulibaly
4433433:knee.note: Coulibaly (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
4433433:knee.long: Coulibaly's rookie year comes to an end due to a knee injury. She'll be looking to take a step forward next year after averaging 5.2 points, 2.6 rebounds and 0.7 steals per game this year for the Sky.

3142010:knee.name: Azura Stevens
3142010:knee.note: Stevens (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics
3142010:knee.long: Steven is sidelined Thursday with a knee injury, ending her regular season. The veteran forward is under contract with the Sky for 2027, and she averaged 10.6 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks per game in 2026.

2529137:knee.name: Natasha Cloud
2529137:knee.note: Cloud (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Mystics.
2529137:knee.long: Cloud is out for the season finale Thursday with a knee injury. The veteran guard is slated to be an unrestricted free agent this winter, having averaged 11.1 points, 4.8 assists, 3.4 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game for the Sky this year.

2491205:knee.name: Skylar Diggins
2491205:knee.note: Diggins (knee) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Sara Jane Gamelli of BallisLife.com reports.
2491205:knee.long: She will now "focus on recovering an aggravated right knee injury." She hadn't played since July 3 and her rehab didn't progress as quickly as she would've hoped. She appeared in 19 games and posted averages of 14.2 points, 3.2 rebounds and 4.9 assists.

4433630:knee.name: Rickea Jackson
4433630:knee.note: The Sky announced Tuesday that Jackson will miss the remainder of the season after suffering a torn ACL in her left knee during Sunday's 86-79 win over the Lynx.
4433630:knee.long: The season-ending knee injury is a devastating development for Jackson and the Sky, as the 25-year-old forward was well on her way to a career-best campaign. Through Chicago's first four games, Jackson averaged 18.0 points, 4.8 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 1.8 blocks and 1.5 three-pointers in 29.5 minutes per contest. After Jackson's early exit in Sunday's contest, Aicha Coulibaly opened the second half with the starters and looks to be the most likely candidate to move into the top unit for the Sky's next game Wednesday versus the Wings.

4433792:knee.name: Rayah Marshall
4433792:knee.note: Marshall has been ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's game against the Tempo due to a right knee injury.
4433792:knee.long: Marshall suffered a knee injury shortly after checking in and won't be able to continue in this one. Nell Angloma could see a few more minutes in Marshall's absence.

4398966:knee.name: Olivia Nelson-Ododa
4398966:knee.note: Nelson-Ododa (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
4398966:knee.long: Nelson-Ododa is sidelined for the regular-season finale with a knee injury. She has one more year left on her deal after averaging a career-high 10.1 points, 5.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists for the Sun in 2026.

4433514:ankle.name: Saniya Rivers
4433514:ankle.note: Rivers (ankle) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
4433514:ankle.long: Rivers is missing the regular-season finale with an ankle injury. She's under contract for next year after averaging 6.9 points, 3.1 assists and 1.1 steals per game over 38 appearances in 2026.

2490553:knee.name: Brittney Griner
2490553:knee.note: Griner (knee) is out for Thursday's game against the Tempo.
2490553:knee.long: Griner is sitting out the regular-season finale due to a knee injury. The veteran center was limited to 18 appearances this year, and she's set for unrestricted free agency this offseason.

3922628:shoulder.name: Kennedy Burke
3922628:shoulder.note: The Sun announced Monday that Burke suffered a sprained AC joint in the FIBA World Cup and will miss the rest of the season.
3922628:shoulder.long: With Connecticut eliminated from playoff contention, Burke is sitting out the remaining four games on the schedule with an eye toward next season. Her absence should allow Nell Angloma and Aaliyah Edwards to handle more playing time. Burke averaged a career-high 8.8 points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.4 assists per contest in 37 games this season.

3913881:lower-leg.name: Alanna Smith
3913881:lower-leg.note: Smith (lower leg) is out for Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs against Golden State on Friday.
3913881:lower-leg.long: Smith will miss the entirely of the first round while nursing a lower leg injury suffered during the FIBA World Cup. Maddy Siegrist and Alysha Clark will once again be asked to step up with Smith sidelined.

4433790:knee.name: Azzi Fudd
4433790:knee.note: Fudd will undergo an arthroscopic procedure to address her right knee soreness and will be sidelined for the remainder of the 2026 season.
4433790:knee.long: Fudd has been sidelined since early August due to her ongoing right knee soreness, and she'll undergo a procedure that will ultimately end her rookie season. Across 30 regular-season appearances (24 starts) this year, she averaged 13.1 points, 1.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds and 1.7 steals in 31.7 minutes per game. In her absence, Odyssey Sims, Alanna Smith and Alysha Clark have seen increased roles, and that trend will likely continue down the stretch as the Wings compete for a playoff berth.

5345473:personal.name: Costanza Verona
5345473:personal.note: Verona's contract was temporarily suspended by the Wings Saturday.
5345473:personal.long: Verona is signed to a developmental contract, so she has only appeared in one regular-season game for Dallas during the 2026 campaign. She will now head overseas, where she will suit up for the Italian National Team for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup. It's unknown whether Verona will be back with the Wings, though her departure will allow the team to sign another player to a developmental deal.

4790263:not-injury-related.name: Iliana Rupert
4790263:not-injury-related.note: Rupert is pregnant, and the Valkyries have filed for a replacement contract ahead of the 2026 season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports Thursday.
4790263:not-injury-related.long: Rupert signed a multi-year contract with Golden State during the offseason and missed the start of training camp due to an overseas commitment. Her status for the 2026 regular season now appears to be in jeopardy due to her pregnancy. The 24-year-old made 21 regular-season appearances (11 starts) for the Valkyries last year and averaged 9.3 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.6 assists in 23.1 minutes per game. If Rupert is sidelined in 2026, Janelle Salaun, Kiah Stokes and Laeticia Amihere are candidates to see increased work.

4065760:leg.name: Tyasha Harris
4065760:leg.note: Harris (leg) will miss the rest of the season, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.
4065760:leg.long: Harris was injured during Thursday's 86-66 win over Minnesota. She was diagnosed with a broken left fibula, though it's unknown if it will affect her heading into the 2027 campaign. The 28-year-old averaged a career-low 4.1 points along with 1.1 rebounds and 2.0 assists over 13.5 minutes per contest in 39 regular-season games, including four starts, in 2026. While Harris wasn't a consistent contributor for Indiana during the season, her absence could at least open the door for a little more involvement from Myisha Hines-Allen and Monique Billings.

4398776:leg.name: NaLyssa Smith
4398776:leg.note: The Aces announced Thursday that Smith will be sidelined for the rest of the season after suffering a non-contact left leg injury during Sunday's game versus the Tempo, per Chelsea Leite of TSN.
4398776:leg.long: It's a big blow for the defending-champion Aces ahead of the postseason. Smith started all 38 of her appearances for Las Vegas, so a spot in the first unit is now open. Brianna Turner appears to the most likely candidate to replace Smith in the starting lineup going forward.

5106170:coach-s-decision.name: Ndjakalenga Mwenentanda
5106170:coach-s-decision.note: Mwenentanda (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
5106170:coach-s-decision.long: Mwenentanda has appeared in her team's last two games, but she'll be shut down for the Sparks' final game of the 2026 campaign. She played in seven games across stops in LA and Golden State this season.

4433808:coach-s-decision.name: Shyanne Sellers
4433808:coach-s-decision.note: Sellers (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Valkyries.
4433808:coach-s-decision.long: Sellers will take a seat for the season finale despite being left off the injury report initially. She appeared in two games for the Sparks after signing a developmental contract in late August.

4433404:ankle.name: Cameron Brink
4433404:ankle.note: Brink (ankle) is listed as out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
4433404:ankle.long: Brink missed the last two games but will now be sidelined for the Sparks' final game of the season. The 24-year-old averaged a career-best 9.5 points along with 5.0 rebounds, 1.5 assists and 1.8 blocks over 19.2 minutes per contest in 31 regular-season games, including one start, throughout the 2026 campaign.

4597509:ankle.name: Aaliyah Nye
4597509:ankle.note: Nye (ankle) has been ruled out for Thursday's game against Golden State.
4597509:ankle.long: Nye will end the campaign with a third consecutive absence due to a left ankle injury. She'll finish the season having averaged 1.0 points in 2.8 minutes per contest across 20 regular-season outings between Los Angeles and Atlanta.

5278237:foot.name: Anastasiia Olairi Kosu
5278237:foot.note: Kosu (foot) has been ruled out for Tuesday's Game 2 of the first round of the playoffs against the Liberty.
5278237:foot.long: Kosu will miss a sixth consecutive contest due to a right foot injury, though her absence shouldn't cause any significant waves in the rotation. If the Lynx manage to stave off elimination Tuesday, the 21-year-old's next opportunity to play will come in Game 3 on Thursday.

5208984:coach-s-decision.name: Elena Buenavida
5208984:coach-s-decision.note: Buenavida (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Fever.
5208984:coach-s-decision.long: Buenavida will take a seat for Thursday's regular-season finale after initially being left off the injury report. She hasn't made an appearance for the Lynx after inking a developmental contract Aug. 11.

4398589:not-injury-related.name: Elizabeth Balogun
4398589:not-injury-related.note: Balogun (not with team) is out for Wednesday's game against the Dream.
4398589:not-injury-related.long: Balogun remains away from the Liberty for the regular-season finale Wednesday. It's unknown if she'll report to the club at any point this postseason.

4698730:coach-s-decision.name: Kara Dunn
4698730:coach-s-decision.note: Dunn (coach's decision) is listed as out for Thursday's game against the Aces.
4698730:coach-s-decision.long: Dunn is signed to a developmental contract and is eligible to appear in up to 12 regular-season contests. She played in the Mercury's last four games, most recently amassing a career-high 11 points in Monday's 87-86 win over Dallas. However, the rookie won't suit up for Phoenix's final game of the year, so she will finish the 2026 campaign with averages of 6.5 points and 1.5 rebounds over 15.0 minutes in four regular-season games. Dunn also shot an efficient 57.1 percent from behind the arc.

3065570:lower-leg.name: Kelsey Plum
3065570:lower-leg.note: Plum (leg) will miss the remainder of the 2026 WNBA season, Alexa Philippou of ESPN.com reports.
3065570:lower-leg.long: Plum is still not feeling the effects of a lingering lower leg injury and will be shut down with the Mercury out of the playoffs. The star guard is set to become a free agent at the conclusion of the season. In five appearances with the Mercury, she averaged 15.8 points and 2.8 assists.

3906769:not-injury-related.name: Jovana Nogic
3906769:not-injury-related.note: Nogic (not injury related) intends to play professionally in Russia and won't return to Phoenix this season, Aya Abdeen of TheIXSports.com reports.
3906769:not-injury-related.long: Nogic had her contract temporarily suspended June 20 and will now be out for the remainder of the WNBA season, as she's slated to compete overseas in Russia with an eye on leading the Serbian national team in the EuroBasket 2027 qualifiers. The guard appeared in 16 games (seven starts) for Phoenix, averaging 10.4 points, 1.6 assists and 1.1 rebounds in 20.2 minutes per contest. With Nogic out of the fold for the foreseeable future, Alexa Held stands to continue benefiting from expanded opportunities in the backcourt.

4433690:back.name: Holly Winterburn
4433690:back.note: Winterburn (back) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against Golden State.
4433690:back.long: Winterburn will be held out of Portland's season finale due to a back injury, and she'll finish the 2026 campaign having averaged 4.0 points, 1.8 assists and 1.4 rebounds across 11.2 minutes per game in 29 regular-season appearances (one start). She began the season on a developmental deal before being converted to a standard contract, and the 25-year-old guard is set to be an unrestricted free agent this season.

5209202:knee.name: Nyadiew Puoch
5209202:knee.note: Puoch (knee) is listed as out for Tuesday's game against Golden State.
5209202:knee.long: Puoch won't be available for the Fire's final game of the 2026 campaign, marking just her second absence of the season. Without Puoch in the mix, Frieda Buhner and Amy Okonkwo could see more action.

5346554:knee.name: Teja Oblak
5346554:knee.note: Oblak (knee) has been ruled out for Tuesday's game against the Valkyries.
5346554:knee.long: Oblak will end the season on the inactive list for a fourth consecutive game due to a left knee injury. The 35-year-old guard made her WNBA debut this year and will finish the 2026 campaign with averages of 5.6 points, 3.2 assists, 1.6 rebounds, 0.8 triples and 0.7 steals while shooting 36.7 percent from downtown across 13.4 minutes per game in 29 regular-season appearances (one start).

4682797:personal.name: Luisa Geiselsoder
4682797:personal.note: Geiselsoder (personal) won't return this season, according to Sean Highkin of RoseGardenReport.com.
4682797:personal.long: Geiselsoder will represent Germany at the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup, and since she's been out of the rotation for a while, she's leaving early for preparation and won't return this season. She ends the season with averages of 4.5 points, 2.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists across 16.6 minutes per game in 21 appearances (nine starts).

4703794:knee.name: Sarah Ashlee Barker
4703794:knee.note: The Fire announced Friday that Barker will undergo surgery to repair a torn ACL and will miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign.
4703794:knee.long: Barker was helped to the locker room in the first quarter of Wednesday's loss to the Wings, and she's now been diagnosed with a season-ending injury. The second-year guard took on a significant role for the Fire after the club selected her in the 2026 WNBA Expansion Draft. Across 26 regular-season games (15 starts), the 24-year-old averaged 10.7 points, 4.5 rebounds, 2.4 assists and 0.9 steals in 24.7 minutes per contest. Karlie Samuelson, Teja Oblak and Nyadiew Puoch are candidates for increased playing time in Barker's stead.

4433795:knee.name: Sania Feagin
4433795:knee.note: Feagin (knee) was diagnosed with a torn left ACL on Thursday and will miss the rest of the 2026 campaign, WNBA reporter Kareem Copeland reports.
4433795:knee.long: Feagin agreed to a developmental contract with Portland on June 24 after spending time in Los Angeles. After appearing in 16 regular-season games for the Sparks in 2025, the 23-year-old played in only three regular-season contests in 2026, logging a combined 10 minutes. Feagin had yet to make her debut with the Fire, though that will now need to wait, assuming Portland keeps her on the roster moving ahead.

5106222:coach-s-decision.name: Taina Mair
5106222:coach-s-decision.note: Mair (coach's decision) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against the Wings.
5106222:coach-s-decision.long: Mair will sit out Seattle's season finale. The developmental player will finish her rookie season with averages of 1.3 points and 0.5 assists in 5.1 minutes per game across 10 regular-season outings.

4432832:knee.name: Zia Cooke
4432832:knee.note: Cooke (knee) has been ruled out for Wednesday's game against Dallas.
4432832:knee.long: Cooke will end the 2026 campaign with a third consecutive absence due to a right knee injury. She'll also finish the season having averaged career-high marks in points (7.5), rebounds (1.7) and assists (1.1) across 15.0 minutes per game in 41 regular-season appearances (one start). She's set to enter restricted free agency this offseason.

3917453:knee.name: Katie Lou Samuelson
3917453:knee.note: The Storm announced Friday that Samuelson underwent successful left knee surgery and will miss the remainder of the season.
3917453:knee.long: Seattle's frontcourt takes another hit after losing Ezi Magbegor to a torn ACL on Thursday. Samuelson had a delayed start to the year due ACL surgery recovery, averaging 4.4 points, 2.1 rebounds and 0.8 assists in 15.3 minutes per contest over 32 games this season. The Storm should lean more heavily on Stefanie Dolson, Mackenzie Holmes and Taylor Thierry the rest of the way.

4398768:knee.name: Nyara Sabally
4398768:knee.note: Sabally recently underwent arthroscopic left knee surgery but is expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 season, Ian Finlayson of Sportsnet.ca reports.
4398768:knee.long: Sabally is coming off a career year with the Tempo, during which she averaged 12.3 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.0 steals and 0.9 blocks across 23.9 minutes per contest. However, she was limited by injuries, appearing in only 24 regular-season games (20 starts). She has already begun her rehab process and will be a restricted free agent this offseason.

5017605:coach-s-decision.name: Kamila Borkowska
5017605:coach-s-decision.note: Borkowska (coach's decision) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
5017605:coach-s-decision.long: Borkowska will be sidelined for her team's final matchup of the regular season. She didn't appear in a game for the Tempo after signing a developmental contract Saturday.

4898548:coach-s-decision.name: Maria Gakdeng
4898548:coach-s-decision.note: Gakdeng is out for Thursday's game against the Sun as a coach's decision.
4898548:coach-s-decision.long: Gakdeng's season is over before she was able to make her debut. She'll look for another developmental opportunity this offseason.

3910470:back.name: Maria Conde
3910470:back.note: Conde (back) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
3910470:back.long: Conde is sitting out the regular-season finale Thursday. The rookie forward is set to be a reserved free agent this winter but should receive a qualifying offer, having averaged 8.5 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game for Toronto in 2026.

2569044:personal.name: Temi Fagbenle
2569044:personal.note: Fagbenle (personal) is out for Thursday's game against the Sun.
2569044:personal.long: Fagbenle won't rejoin the team for the regular-season finale due to personal reasons. She's set for unrestricted free agency this offseason, having averaged 5.9 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.0 assists for the Tempo this year.

3904576:hip.name: Marina Mabrey
3904576:hip.note: Mabrey (hip) will miss the final four games of the 2026 season, Zulfi Sheikh of Sportsnet reports.
3904576:hip.long: Mabrey, who has been sidelined since mid-August, will not require surgery and is expected to make a full recovery ahead of the 2027 WNBA season. Across 32 appearances, she produced averages of 20.8 points, 3.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 0.9 steals.

4684384:knee.name: Aneesah Morrow
4684384:knee.note: Morrow (knee) will miss the rest of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.
4684384:knee.long: Brittney Sykes (foot) will also miss the final eight games for Toronto. According to coach Sandy Brondello, Morrow is not facing a lengthy recovery. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole are candidates to step into larger roles the rest of the way.

2988756:foot.name: Brittney Sykes
2988756:foot.note: Sykes (foot) will miss the remainder of the 2026 season, Chelsea Leite of TSN reports.
2988756:foot.long: This is a tough blow for Toronto, but Sykes' foot issues have continued to linger. She will finish the campaign with averages of 18.6 points, 3.5 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.2 steals and 0.5 blocks in 29.4 minutes per contest. Kia Nurse and Ornella Bankole could see larger roles the rest of the way with this news.
